sizeUnit.description: A proposal's size unit: the base asset, or the pair's quote currency.

access-key.key.description: One key as GET /api/v1/keys lists it. `lastUsedAt` is the key's last request, null when never used; gcx writes it to disk at most once a minute and at shutdown, so after a crash it can be older than the key's real last use. `revokedAt` is null for a key in use. `limits` and `suspendedAt` (Amendment 1) are always sent by this version.

limits.description: A trading key's limits; null until set (it then acts on nothing), and for a key that does not trade. Absent from an answer of a version before keys traded: null.

suspendedAt.description: When a person suspended the key (A10); null while it runs. Absent from an answer of a version before keys traded: null.

access-key.limits.description: A trading key's limits (Amendment 1 A4), set only by a person, in force from the key's next command. `accounts`: the account ids it may trade, or `all` for every account held now or added later. `markets`: the instruments it may trade, each by its exact id (the key form offers every perpetual), or `all` for every market on those accounts, whatever it is quoted in. `perOrder`: the largest order value in USDC at the runtime's price. `per24h`: the most in USDC of what the key's orders that add risk filled in the last 24 hours plus what of them is open now (RULINGS 74 (b): a cancelled order gives its value back). `leverage`: the highest leverage on a market where the key adds risk. Decimal strings; the panel pre-fills 1000, 10000 and 5 (the owner's defaults).

access-key.list.description: GET /api/v1/keys: every key made on this runtime, revoked ones included, oldest first.

access-key.notifications.description: Optional accepted-command notices; absent means off. Proposals are always notified independently. Retained after revocation.

access-key.revoke.description: POST /api/v1/keys/{keyId}/revoke: an empty object. The key is refused (401) from its next request, and, as Suspend does, its resting orders that would open or add to a position are cancelled. Answers the key, or 404 for a key that does not exist or is already revoked.

access-key.setLimits.description: POST /api/v1/keys/{keyId}/limits: a trading key's new limits, in force from its next command. Answers the key, or 404 for a key that does not exist or is revoked.

access-key.setScope.description: POST /api/v1/keys/{keyId}/scope: the key's new scope, in force from its next request. Answers the key, or 404 for a key that does not exist or is revoked.

access-key.suspend.description: POST /api/v1/keys/{keyId}/suspend and /resume: an empty object. Suspend (Amendment 1 A10, RULINGS 73 (a)): the key's writes are refused (403 "Suspended by you") from its next command, its reads continue, and its resting orders that would open or add to a position are cancelled; its take-profits, stop-losses, reduce-only orders and positions stay. Resume lets it write again. Answers the key, or 404 for a key that does not exist or is revoked.

accounts-api.add.description: POST /api/v1/accounts/add: add a sub-account or a vault that `found` offers, or (additive, 0003b amendment 2 v2) a main account whose API wallet stands in gcx: its own account, added, or brought back with its history. A fresh read must list it; it then trades at once, its orders signed by its main account's API wallet with its address as `vaultAddress`, with gcx's builder fee as the main account's. Answers 200 `{sourceId}` (the same requestId or the same address again answers the same), with `warning` (additive, 0013 amendment 2 d5) when gcx already trades as many accounts as Hyperliquid last accepted live, so this one will be polled: "Hyperliquid allows a limited number of live accounts per connection point; this one updates every minute over the slower path, which can also delay its orders."; 422 `{rejected, text}`: `not-found` (Hyperliquid does not list it), `most` (gcx trades up to 100 accounts at once, 0013 d13), `not-available`; 409: the requestId was used for another account; 503: Hyperliquid could not be read.

accounts-api.agent.description: An API wallet as Hyperliquid lists it (`extraAgents`): its name ("" for the one unnamed wallet), its address, and Hyperliquid's expiry (null: none). `held`: gcx's key store holds its key on this computer; the panel shows such a wallet but never offers to replace it.

accounts-api.connect.description: POST /api/v1/accounts: connect the main account whose wallet the panel connected. `label`: the account's name in gcx, at most 50 characters; empty takes the default (Hyperliquid, then Hyperliquid-2, Hyperliquid-3, as goodcryptoX). `referral`: the referral line was shown and left checked (stored `pending`, sent once by gcx's API wallet after it is active); false when unchecked, not shown, or already referred (stored `declined`). `replace`: only when the wallet check said `full`, the name of the API wallet the person picked to replace; its old key stops working. The same main account sent again ("Try again", or after a reload) answers the same account and the same API wallet; another main account connects beside those already there, with its own record and its own API wallet (several main accounts; a main account still waiting for its approval stays).

accounts-api.connected.description: The answer to POST /api/v1/accounts: the account's id in gcx and its API wallet's name and address, nothing else. The key is on disk, encrypted, before this answer is sent. 422 `{rejected, text}`: not a main account's wallet, slots full without a pick, a pick that is not offered; 409: the requestId was used for another main account; 503: Hyperliquid could not be read, or the key store is locked or has no unlock source.

accounts-api.feeState.description: The builder-fee approval for gcx's 0.03 % (decision 0007 d20): `approved` when Hyperliquid's `maxBuilderFee` for our builder is at least 30 (tenths of a basis point; an old approval of 1 % reads 1000 and stands), `not approved` below it, `unknown` when it could not be read (the accounts list reads every approval not read as approved before it answers, so there `unknown` means the read failed). Every order carries the fee, exits, closes and stop-losses included (ruling 5). `not approved` refuses a new order or bot (422 `builder-fee`), for a person and a key alike, after one fresh read of the approval that still says so (MH 196; a read that fails is `unknown` and nothing is refused); a Close, an order that only reduces, a cancel, an exit and a Stop are not refused, and a running bot goes on. Hyperliquid refuses an order that carries the fee when the approval is gone.

accounts-api.found.description: GET /api/v1/accounts/found: the sub-accounts and the vaults each active main account may add, read fresh from Hyperliquid (`subAccounts` and `leadingVaults` of the main account), less those already in gcx. `name`: Hyperliquid's; `master`: the main account's sourceId. With `?master={sourceId}` (additive, 0003b amendment 1): that one active main account's whole list, including those in gcx, each of those carrying `sourceId` (active, waiting or being removed; a removed one has none, it is offered); 404 for an unknown or inactive main account. With `?master=`, since 0003b amendment 2 v2 (additive), the first item is the main account itself (kind `master`: its gcx name, or the one it would get, and its sourceId while it is in gcx), and `master` names the API wallet's id (a main account's id names its wallet too). Answers 503 when Hyperliquid could not be read.

sourceId.description: Additive: only with `?master=`, the account's id when it is in gcx.

accounts-api.inPortfolio.description: Only the pressed Dashboard membership switch; merged per account, person only (0007 Amendment 6)

accounts-api.remove.description: POST /api/v1/accounts/{sourceId}/remove (0003b d12; RULINGS 23; 0003b amendment 3, ruling 413): gcx removes the account from itself and leaves Hyperliquid as it is: resting orders rest, positions stay, nothing is cancelled or closed; its bots stop with the reason Account removed and its internal stops are no longer watched. `trading`: the dialog's Keep trading history (unticked by default): kept, its bots and orders stay in the lists marked Account removed; unticked, they leave every view at once, for good. `portfolio`: written true (no box since amendment 3; read by nothing). `revoke` on the first call (added 2026-10-10): Also remove the API wallet from Hyperliquid (unticked by default): the remove then waits for the main wallet's revoke (approveAgent to the zero address under its name, relayed by `signed` on the wallet's id) to be seen done, the other accounts under the wallet meeting line 13 (their new orders refused, a running bot stopping at its next refused send); absent (an older client), the revoke is asked only for the last account under the main. Journaled (`source.removing`) before anything is sent. Every account goes alone (ruling 219). The key is deleted with the last account under the wallet. `revoke: false` sent again on an account while it is removing is the person's Remove without revoking, for that account.

accounts-api.removed.description: Where a remove stands: `removing` with the row's `waiting` and `revoke` (the panel asks the main wallet for the revoke while `revoke` is true: the last account under its main), or `removed`, with `warning` when something stays on Hyperliquid: an account removed while others under its main stay (the main account's API wallet can still trade it until the last of them leaves gcx), or the last one removed without the revoke (the API wallet stays approved until it expires or is removed there; an earlier export archive still holds the key).

accounts-api.rename.description: POST /api/v1/accounts/{sourceId}/rename (0003b d1; goodcryptoX's exchange-rename.vue): the account's name in gcx, 1 to 50 characters; names may repeat. The panel sends nothing for an empty field (no change). Answers 200 `renamed`; 400 an empty or longer name; 404 an account not in gcx (or removed).

accounts-api.renamed.description: The answer to a rename: the account and its name now.

accounts-api.renew.description: POST /api/v1/accounts/{sourceId}/renew (0003b d12 replace / reissue; goodcryptoX's Update API wallet automatically): no fields. A main account that trades gets a new API wallet key, kept on disk before the answer (`connected`: the same name, the new address; the same key again while it waits). Its own wallet then approves it through `signed` (approveAgent under the same name, which replaces the old API wallet on Hyperliquid); the old key signs until a fresh read of Hyperliquid lists the new one. 404 not a main account in gcx; 422 `not-available` while its first API wallet waits for approval (Try again) or while it is being removed; 503 when the key could not be kept. Added 2026-10-04.

accounts-api.row.description: One element of GET /api/v1/accounts. The first five fields are the account selector's (0007); the rest are added by roadmap A8 for the connect screens and the Settings rows: `enabled` is true once Hyperliquid listed the API wallet (the account trades from then on; until then it waits for approval). `agent.approval`: `waiting` until Hyperliquid lists the API wallet, then `active`. `agent.validUntil`: Hyperliquid's expiry from gcx's last read (null: none; absent: not read since gcx started). `builderFee.stale`: the last read failed and `state` is the one before it. `referral`: `pending` until gcx's API wallet has sent Hyperliquid's referral code once, then `sent`, or `declined` (unchecked, already referred, or refused by Hyperliquid).

master.description: A sub-account's or vault's main account (its sourceId) while the main account is in gcx, else its API wallet's id (0003b amendment 2 v2); absent on a main account.

state.description: goodcryptoX's account status code (ok, AuthenticationError, …); absent reads ok.

agent.description: The API wallet that signs for this account: its main account's, one per main account. Since 0003b amendment 2 v2 (2026-10-05, additive) on every account under that main, the main's own included, where it was on a main account's row only.

id.description: Additive (amendment 2 v2): the API wallet's own id, which `signed`, `renew` and `found?master=` take; one renewal or revoke on it acts for every account under its main.

master.description: Additive (amendment 2 v2): the main account's address, whose wallet approves, renews and revokes this API wallet.

moved.description: Deprecated, never sent since 0024 amendment 3 (an import keeps the API wallets with no hold); builds before it sent true for an account brought from another machine whose API wallet waited for a replacement. Absent: not moved.

key.description: Additive (unlock-retry, 0008 amendment 4): present while this account's API wallet key cannot sign. `state`: `locked` (the key store cannot be opened; goodcryptoX keeps trying), `elsewhere` (it was sealed under another Windows account or on another computer: no try here can open it), `missing` (this computer has no key for it: no key store file, or a new store without it). `replace`: Replace API wallet (`renew`) is offered as the last resort: at once for `missing` and `elsewhere`; for `locked` once a whole schedule of tries failed or the last start failed too. The replacement makes a new key store where the old one cannot be opened, and every other main account's key in it is then `missing`. `cause`: what the last try met (`timeout`; `refused`; `profile`, before the Windows account was loaded; `blocked`, the tool could not be started). `why`: the reason as the log wrote it, never a path or a secret. `id`, `master`: the API wallet's id and its main account's address, whose wallet approves the replacement.

budget.description: Additive (0003 Amendment 2 d1, d8; 2026-10-05): the account's request allowance as Hyperliquid's `userRateLimit` read it (at most once a minute; the list reads it when asked): 10,000 plus 1 per 1 USDC traded, never refilling with time; once used up Hyperliquid allows one request every 10 seconds. Absent before a read or when the read failed.

surplus.description: `nRequestsSurplus`, shown raw; its meaning is pin R4.

cumVlm.description: USDC traded since the address began.

at.description: When it was read, ms since the epoch.

refused.description: Deprecated (0003 Amendment 2 d7, 2026-10-05): never sent any more. It said a sub-account or a vault took no new order or bot after Hyperliquid refused gcx's builder fee there; now each order carries the fee and Hyperliquid answers each one. Kept in the schema for one release, as the no-breaking-changes rule asks.

wallet.description: Additive (MH 2026-10-05, audit line 13): the main account's API wallet, which signs for this account, has expired or is no longer listed at Hyperliquid, as the runtime's last read found it; a new order or bot on it is refused 422 `api-wallet` with the sentence, and the panel shows the sentence in place of Buy, Sell and Launch. Nothing is held: a running bot's next order goes to the exchange, which refuses it. Absent: neither, or no runtime is open.

simulated.description: true on a demo account (docs/panel/demo-accounts.md; always listed, after the connected accounts): made up, it never trades and nothing of it reaches a venue; its lists are the socket's `demo/` topics. Absent on a connected account.

live.description: Additive (0013 amendment 2 d5): true while the account gets live updates; false while it is polled, because Hyperliquid allows only so many live accounts per internet address (gcx follows what Hyperliquid accepts) and accounts with a bot or an order of gcx come first. Absent: the runtime does not say (no account open yet, a demo account).

everyMs.description: Additive (0013 amendment 2 d5): while `live` is false, how often the account is read (ms): at least a minute, longer when many accounts are polled. Absent while live.

open.description: Additive (2026-10-03; 0003b d12, RULINGS 23): gcx's bots running and orders not done on the account, which a remove leaves on Hyperliquid unwatched (the remove dialog's warning); also the main account's near-empty warning (a sub-account with a bot). Absent when no runtime is open.

resting.description: Additive (2026-10-10, 0003b amendment 3 d5): of `orders`, those resting on Hyperliquid (the remove dialog's count of orders still open there).

held.description: Additive (2026-10-10, 0003b amendment 3 d5): of `orders`, the stops and trails gcx watches itself, which end with a remove (the dialog's clause) or can no longer be sent when the API wallet goes.

removing.description: Additive (2026-10-03; 0003b d12): the account's remove is under way. `waiting`: its sends (and those of the accounts leaving with it when its API wallet ends) that Hyperliquid has not answered yet; it ends when that is 0 and, when it awaits the API wallet's revoke, once Hyperliquid no longer lists gcx's API wallet (`revoke`: this account's remove asks the revoke, its box ticked or, on a remove before the box, the last account under the main; false after the person's Remove without revoking). Absent when not being removed.

accounts-api.rows.description: GET /api/v1/accounts. With no account connected: `[]` (200, never 404), and the rest of what the panel reads answers empty too: the settings their defaults, the history an empty page (`{rows: []}`), the `orders`, `positions` and `bots` topics an empty snapshot, and `account-state`, `balances` and `leverage/…` are accepted and send nothing until an account exists; market data is served as always.

accounts-api.signed.description: POST /api/v1/accounts/{sourceId}/signed: one action the main wallet signed, as Hyperliquid's `/exchange` takes it (the typed data as the builder-fees page builds it: domain HyperliquidSignTransaction, `signatureChainId` the wallet's own chain, one nonce for the action and the body). gcx relays it, field for field, only when its allow-list admits it: `approveAgent` for exactly the address and name gcx made for this account, and `approveBuilderFee` for gcx's builder at exactly "0.03%". While every account under the wallet is being removed, only `approveAgent` to the zero address under its API wallet's name (the revoke); while an account under a wallet that stands is being removed with `revoke` true (0003b amendment 3 d3), that revoke as well as the usual approvals. Anything else is refused 422 `not-allowed` and nothing is sent. Answers 200 `{accepted: true}` when Hyperliquid accepted it; 422 `{rejected: "venue", text}` with Hyperliquid's text; 503 `{error, text}` when Hyperliquid did not answer (it may have taken it: the accounts list shows what it did); `text` is the sentence to show, `error` carries the cause.

accounts-api.wallet.description: GET /api/v1/accounts/wallet/{address}: what the connect screen needs after the wallet is connected (step 1), read fresh from Hyperliquid. `role` must be `user` to connect (a sub-account, a vault or an API wallet shows "Connect the wallet that owns the Hyperliquid account"; `missing`, a wallet Hyperliquid does not know, shows "Wallet not linked to Hyperliquid, or the account has < 5 USDC"). `name`: the API wallet name gcx will use, the first of gcx, gcx1, gcx2 that Hyperliquid does not list; null when `full`. `full`: the named API wallets fill the account's slots (3, plus 2 per sub-account; the unnamed one is not counted) or all three names are taken: the person picks one to replace from `agents` (never one with `held`), and the connect body names it in `replace`; nothing is signed until one is picked. `validUntil`: the expiry to sign into `approveAgent` (`<name> valid_until <validUntil>`), Hyperliquid's clock plus 180 days less one hour, never this computer's clock. `referred`: whether Hyperliquid's `referral` read shows a referrer (null: the read failed); the referral line is shown only when it is false. `builderFee.max` is null when the read failed. Answers 503 when the role, the API wallets, the sub-accounts or Hyperliquid's clock could not be read.

affiliate-api.clear.description: C77: internal-only local test reset. No permanent referral, installation/report or fee record is rewritten.

affiliate-api.figures.description: GET /api/v1/partner/figures (decision 0021 amendment 4 d6): per code of the stored partner key, read from goodcryptoX's partner-code server, at most once a minute and only when the page asks. 404 with no key that verifies, the internal test key, no server, or a server that does not serve figures yet; 503 {error} when the server cannot be read and nothing is kept. Counts and sums only: nothing names an installation, an address or an account.

through.description: The last UTC day the volume is counted through (ruling 108 (a)); null before any day is counted.

at.description: When the server's answer was received (Unix ms).

stale.description: True when the server could not be read now and the last answer received is served.

codes.description: One entry per discount from 0 to the key's maximum, in order.

discount.description: The code's discount, a percent of gcx's fee (as GET /api/v1/partner names it).

joined.description: Users who joined with this code.

trading.description: Of those, the ones whose orders reached the server this week (from Monday 00:00 UTC).

volume.description: This week's paid volume per unit, a day or two behind (the trades that pay, as goodcryptoX counts them to pay); empty when none. The main collateral first, then by name.

affiliate-api.install.description: POST /api/v1/partner: a partner key, as pasted. Valid when every code in it verifies against our key; it replaces the one stored. 422 {error: "Invalid key"}. Internal startup tier accepts the exact typed text as a separate local sample key, without verification or server effects.

affiliate-api.join.description: POST /api/v1/referral: a partner's code, as pasted (whitespace around it is trimmed). Verified offline against our key; stored once, never changed or removed. 422 {error: "Invalid code"} or {error: "You can't refer yourself"} (this gcx's own partner key has the code's partner number); 409 {error: "You're already referred"}. Internal startup tier accepts the exact typed text into separate test metadata, without verification or server effects.

affiliate-api.partner.description: GET /api/v1/partner, and the answer of POST: this gcx's partner key, or {key: null} when none is installed.

max.description: His maximum share, a percent of gcx's fee.

valid.description: False when the key was made under a signing key this version no longer trusts (a rotation): no code is shown; ask goodcryptoX for a new key.

codes.description: One code per discount from 0 to the maximum in 10 % steps; empty when not valid.

key.description: The partner key's text, for Copy partner key.

test.description: Internal local sample key only; never a verified server key.

affiliate-api.referral.description: GET /api/v1/referral, and the answer of POST: the code this gcx joined with and what it changes. Without a code: code null, discount "0", fee "0.03", since null.

code.description: The code's text (gcx- and 99 characters); null before one is entered.

discount.description: The discount on gcx's fee the code gives, a percent of the fee.

fee.description: gcx's builder fee on every order from the next one on, a percent of the trade (0.03 without a code, 0.027 with a 10 % code).

since.description: When the code was entered (Unix ms); null before.

test.description: True only for an internal local test overlay; no effect on actual fees. Absent on older builds.

bot-row.title: Bot row
bot-row.description: One DCA bot as the `bots` topic carries it (decision 0016 §3.1, §8.2; roadmap B9): its state as the reducer holds it (src/domain/dca/live.ts), its own position and PnL, its counters and settings, written by the runtime from the bot's fold (src/runtime/bots/view.ts). Total PnL = realizedPnl + unrealizedPnl + funding. Mirrors src/panel/model/frames.ts (BotRow).

removed.description: Added 2026-10-10 (0003b amendment 3 d1, rulings 339 and 413.3): the row's account is being removed from gcx or was removed with its trading history kept; the bot takes no command. Absent otherwise.

account.description: Added 2026-10-10 (0003b amendment 3 d1): with `removed`, the account's name (shown "<name> (Account removed)"), since its row in the accounts list is gone.

released.description: Added 2026-10-10 (0003b amendment 3 d2, ruling 413.4): with done error, the bot's account was removed from gcx; its line reads Account removed. Absent otherwise.

side.description: The cycle's side, or the one the settings fix; absent for a signal bot before its first signal.

name.description: The person's name for the bot (catalogue E11): set at creation (B8), changed by modify (B65).

note.description: The person's note on the bot.

done.description: Why a done bot ended. adl (added 2026-10-05, decision 0016 Amendment 3): stopped by the exchange's auto-deleveraging, as liquidated by its liquidation. error (added 2026-10-05, MH audit line 13): the exchange refused one of its orders for the account's API wallet (expired or no longer approved) and the bot stopped as goodcryptoX's error stop did, its text in `error`. dust (added 2026-10-02): a spot buy's fee taken in the coin left less than one size step, nothing more was to be bought, and the bot ended holding it.

error.description: Added 2026-10-05 (MH audit line 13): with done error, the exchange's text that stopped the bot; also (RULINGS 218 b) while the bot waits in repair on the exchange's refusal of its spot sale of the rest, that refusal's text.

why.description: Added 2026-10-05 (ruling 203): with `error`, our explanation of what the error was, in the person's language (the `language` setting; English when none is chosen or the language has no text for it); the exchange's own words stay raw in `error`. Absent without `error`; a reader that does not know it shows `error` alone.

paused.description: Added 2026-10-04 (ruling 73 (a)): the trading key that created the bot is suspended or revoked; the bot adds nothing (its entry and averaging orders cancelled, a new cycle waits) and keeps its take-profit, stop-loss and closes. Absent: not paused.

repair.description: 0016 d15: new risk withheld until the person chooses: the bot's own reasons and its orders the order reducer holds in REPAIR. Absent: not in repair.

reasons.description: key-limit (added 2026-10-04): the trading key that created the bot cannot start the next cycle: its limits have no room for it (the 24 hours, the largest order, the account or the market; rulings 109 2 (a), 171 (a)); the bot goes on by itself as soon as they have room (ruling 170 (b)). differs (added 2026-10-05, decision 0016 Amendment 2): the exchange's position differs from the bots' records and the item is open (`attention`).

waitingPrice.description: Added 2026-10-05 (MH's audit list line 4 iii): gcx has had no price of the bot's coin since it started or woke, and the bot's entry, averaging orders or timer wait for one; it goes on by itself at the first price. A status, not a repair. Absent: not waiting for a price.

attention.description: Deprecated with 0028 d18 (stream 2, 2026-10-06; never in a public release, but it is in the test dmgs 6145 and 6272; the Dashboard shows no bot item, no exit-rest row of a bot and no waiting rest of the person until stream 3): no longer sent; the runtime topic's `bot` row carries every item of the bot, this one included. A runtime before it: added 2026-10-05 (decision 0016 Amendment 2, replacing the warning of MH's audit list line 33): "Only gcx trades this coin" is on and the exchange's position on the coin (on spot, the holding) differs from the sum of gcx's bots' records there on two trusted reads 90 s apart: the bot paused its new orders and waits for the person's choice. key: the episode's (the Dashboard's Needs your attention row; POST /api/v1/attention/done); exchange: the exchange's signed size as confirmed; since: the last agreement; done: the Dashboard row was hidden by its Done (the bot stays paused). Absent while nothing differs and on a done bot.

position.description: The bot's own count of its current cycle (0016 d11), not the exchange's.

unrealizedPnl.description: The cycle's position at the runtime's latest price against its average.

funding.description: Paid negative, received positive: the sum of its cycles' funding (src/domain/dca/live.ts Iteration.funding), each payment on its account and coin split by the bot's share of the account's position (0016 Amendment 1 B64).

fees.description: Exchange fees of every fill of the bot's orders: the venue's fee less the part that is gcx's platform fee (platformFees). Negative for a maker whose rebate (Hyperliquid pays rebates as negative fees) is larger than the exchange's part.

platformFees.description: Added in A46. gcx's platform fee of every fill of the bot's orders (Hyperliquid's builderFee, src/domain/dca/live.ts Iteration.platformFees). The venue's fee includes it, so realizedPnl already has both fees and platformFees taken out.

invested.description: goodcryptoX's Invested (EN algo.dcaInvestedInfo): the largest notional of a cycle's entry and averaging orders, over every cycle; the base of the percentages.

apr.description: goodcryptoX's APR: the realized PnL including funding (exchange and platform fees already inside trading PnL) over Invested, a year's worth at the rate since the bot was made, in percent, as of the row.

investedPeak.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10, Max reached): the most the bot had at one time in its position (its cycles' cost at their entry prices, the current cycle and the parts still to close, fees outside) and in its entry and averaging orders resting on the exchange (each at its price × what is left of it; a take-profit or a stop-loss counts for nothing). Absent while not positive.

investedAverage.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10, Average): what the bot had in its position and its resting entry and averaging orders (as investedPeak counts them) on average over its running time (from its creation to its end, else the row's time); time with nothing counts as nothing. Moves with time: also in the bots topic's refresh. Absent while not positive.

aprPeak.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10): `apr` on investedPeak instead of Invested. Moves with time: also in the refresh. Absent with investedPeak, and while no time ran.

aprAverage.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10): `apr` on investedAverage instead of Invested; the running time cancels, so it is the yearly rate while money was held, unmoved while the bot holds nothing. Moves with time: also in the refresh. Absent with investedAverage.

ownFunds.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10): Invested in own funds, the largest of a cycle's entry and averaging orders' notional divided by that cycle's leverage (read at its entry; a cycle before the bot's first known leverage takes that one). Perpetuals only; absent on spot, before any leverage is known, and while not positive.

ownFundsPeak.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10): investedPeak in own funds, each cycle's cost and resting orders divided by its leverage. As ownFunds, absent on spot, before any leverage is known, and while not positive.

ownFundsAverage.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0016 Amendment 10): investedAverage in own funds. Moves with time: also in the refresh. As ownFunds, absent on spot, before any leverage is known, and while not positive.

breakeven.description: B18: the current cycle's take-profit was moved to break-even (its average plus the fees paid so far).

change.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 726 (e)): the current cycle's take-profit's `change` (order-row.schema.json): the last command since the runtime started that moved it (Move to break even) and how it ended at the exchange. Absent while not known, and after a restart.

scale.description: A2 d69: the current cycle's journaled sizing factor; absent in older rows means one

startedAt.description: Added 2026-10-17 (MH 706 (a)): when the bot really started: at its creation with no start time, else when its start time came or Start now was pressed. Absent only while it waits for its start (derived by the fold, so a bot any build started has it).

cycleAt.description: When the current iteration's first entry was made.

pastStop.description: Added 2026-10-17 (MH 623 (f)): the current cycle's stop, worked out from the expected loss (settings slLossPct), comes before averaging orders `from` to `to`, which the cycle does not place; `spot` on a spot pair, where no leverage moves it. Absent otherwise. The details and the Dashboard's Worth a look name them.

endedAt.description: First transition to done, retained on replay; absent on older rows

leverage.description: d100(b): the last recorded grid leverage, served even while its position is flat; absent on spot or an older grid

gridProfitUnit.description: Unit of Grid profit; absent in older rows means quote

gridProfitCoin.description: Retained coin from completed round trips; absent means zero

gridProfitQuote.description: Quote ledger contribution used in Total

trailing.description: Added 2026-10-28 (0040 amendment 6): the trailing exits' running sums, decimal strings in the quote: `gain` = Σ per fill of a trailing exit (fill − level) × size in the exit's favour − the fee paid + the platform fee × level ÷ fill; `value` = Σ level × size. What trailing earned against limit exits = gain + the account's maker rate × value. Absent until a trailing exit fills (both zero)

coinFeePct.description: Grid on spot: the coin-fee percent a buy level's size is grossed up by (the size the grid rests for that level is the plan divided by one minus this); absent means the default rate. Additive: the previous build ignores it and reads the row as before

case.title: Case
case.description: One case (decision 0020 d1-d4): a bounded slice of the journal around one event, the exact exchange traffic around it (with the d3 replacements), a snapshot of the account at that moment and a small header. The same object serves the person's timeline, the API and MCP view, the automatic report and the person's own send. Anonymisation is enforced by the redactor (src/domain/cases/redact.ts: the per-source, by-path rules of $defs/fieldRules and the free-text pass over every other string leaf), its two tests (tests/cases/allowlist.test.ts walks every field of the corpus, the fake-venue scenarios and the recorded fixtures; tests/cases/redact.test.ts searches a recorded case for every secret) and the last check on the finished case (d4.5: no 0x + 40 hex but the builder address, no known address; run by the runtime and again by the Worker). This schema closes the header, the snapshot and the exchange lines; it does not see inside a redacted entry or a body. Money stays decimal strings. Never: a key, a signature, an account address, a balance, an account's dollar total, an account's label, a Telegram id. Version 1 (unreleased; 0020 v2 and v2.1's changes are folded in); a new field is additive and optional (CLAUDE.md, no breaking changes).

id.description: c:<random> for a stored case (opened on a trigger, or sent by the person: a send mints its own, so two sends of one order are two cases); order:<id> or bot:<id> for one built on demand by "What happened?" (d9), never stored under it. A bot's order id holds slashes (<bot>/<iteration>/<role>). runtime is the unstored look at this installation's state and recent redacted log (0020 amendment 2), also built by Send to gcx on a failure line (unlock-retry).

note.description: The person's optional line on "Send to gcx" (d10), after the free-text pass of d3; kept as written otherwise (an e-mail address the person adds included).

demo.description: A demo account (src/runtime/demo.ts): never a trigger, shown only in a case the person builds.

seq.description: The row's seq in the ledger (journal-row.schema.json).

say.description: The row's sentence as 0009 renders it (d1.8): the template id and variables from fromStep, taken by replaying the journal at build time; variables under their own list, fieldRules.sayVars (d3 Table A3), the rest through the free-text pass. Absent for a row that makes no 0009 event (the timeline then uses case.row.<type>).

crash.description: Only on a crash case (d6 T6): the uncaught error as the dying process wrote it (the handler writes the note synchronously and exits with code 1), through the free-text pass, file paths cut to the bundle's own.

page.description: Only on a case of the runtime's own page (d6 T4, template `runtime.page`): the sentence the person was paged with, or the status line that failed (unlock-retry: the line, then on the next line what is behind it, the reason as the log wrote it); on the runtime's case built on demand (`runtime`), the failure lines shown then. Each account's name (its label) replaced by its reference, then through the free-text pass of d3.

runtime.description: Only a runtime case the person asks for (0020 amendment 2); every log item and status text has passed Table A4 and the log text redactor. No journal or traffic is read.

log.description: Last 1,000 log lines at most, oldest first, redacted by field name (A4). Unknown fields retain only their shape; torn lines retain kind and byte count.

case.accountRef.description: An account as gcx's own local id of it (the source id, src/runtime/accounts.ts:129), never its address. Every 0x address of 40 hex digits the account is known by is replaced by this; an address gcx does not know becomes a:unknown<n>, numbered within the case.

case.exchange.description: One line of the wire log (d5) inside the window: a request out, an answer in, or a stream frame in.

n.description: Pairs a request with its answer.

kind.description: The /info or action type (orderStatus, order, cancelByCloid…) or the stream channel (orderUpdates, userFills, user (a userEvents frame), userFundings, error).

status.description: HTTP status of an answer; null: no answer (transport failure or timeout).

ms.description: From the request to its answer.

body.description: Present when the kind is collectable (d3 table B) and the text is at most 256 KiB: the exact text with only the fieldRules.wire replacements and the free-text pass made in place; every other byte, including the digits of every number, as it went or came. A body that is not JSON is one free-text leaf, cut to 2,000 characters.

shape.description: Present instead of body for a shape-only kind that refused or erred, and for a collectable body over 256 KiB (with bodyOver): the JSON's keys with every value replaced by its type name.

error.description: The transport's failure or the parser's refusal text, through the free-text redaction.

acct.description: gcx's account of this line where known (d5.2): the signer's account for a write, the user of an /info read, the subscription's account for a frame. A case takes lines of its subject's account and lines without one.

bodyOver.description: The body passed 256 KiB and is kept as shape and bytes (d2.2).

app.description: The build stamp as 0008 defines it (0008 amendment 1 d9 today; the version and build number of RULINGS section 21 are an 0008 amendment, not this design).

os.description: System name and release, e.g. darwin 25.1.0.

install.description: The install reference: the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256("gcx-case-install:" + installId). The only identifier; shown to the person in Settings so a deletion can be asked for.

policy.description: The collection policy's version in force (d12).

tier.description: The tier the copy says it is (0030 amendments 1 and 2): Internal, Beta or Everyone, from its own label, so a report from an internal tester is told from one that touches production. Optional: absent when the copy reads none (a checkout, a build from before the tiers).

origin.description: auto: opened by a trigger; asked: built by the person's "What happened?"; request: built for one of our signed requests (d11).

kind.description: d6 T1-T10: rejected T1, unknown and not-placed T2, exchange-error T3, notify-alert and notify-page T4, journal-only T5, crash T6, refusal T7, unreachable T8, cut T9 (a bound that cut an order: an Ioc partly filled, a remainder), approval-error T10 (an exchange error on a wallet-signed approval through the signed route); asked and request are origins of cases not opened by a trigger.

class.description: src/venues/hyperliquid/errors.ts ErrorClass. UPGRADE_GATE added 2026-10-05 (0003 Amendment 3 d5): a placement refused in the post-only minutes after an upgrade.

pattern.description: The registry row that matched (errors.ts MESSAGES), absent for UNKNOWN.

status.description: A venue order status (errors.ts STATUSES) or an HTTP status.

template.description: The 0009 template id of a notify trigger.

occurrences.description: Occurrences of the same signature joined into this case (d7).

more.description: Occurrences of the same signature on other subjects joined here after the day's 20 cases of that signature (d7.1).

answering.description: The transport's last request was answered (errors.ts Unreachable).

clockOffsetMs.description: This computer's clock minus the exchange's at the last start-up check (src/runtime/supervisor/startup.ts:157); null when never measured.

trimmed.description: What the size budget (d2) left out.

wireKept.description: False when the window reaches past what the wire log still holds (d5; an order older than 7 days, d9.2) or the log did not exist (before S2); the case then has no exchanges for that part.

case.redactedEntry.description: A journal entry (an engine input, src/domain/orders/engine.ts Input; a runtime entry, runtime-entry.schema.json; a bot entry, bot-entry.schema.json) as journaled, with $defs/fieldRules.journal applied by path and the free-text pass over every other string leaf that is not exact (d3). Open here: the allow-list walk over values (d4.2) and the last check (d4.5) bound it, not this schema. Ticks: at most the last of each 5 s and the one before each send (d1).

case.shape.description: A JSON value's shape: a type name, or an object or array of shapes (an array as its first item's shape).

case.snapshot.description: Everything live on the subject's account at the trigger (B60; MH 2026-09-28, knowledge/v1-package-notes-2026-09-28.md:563): every open order, every bot, every position. Sizes in coin; no balance, margin, value or profit in dollars; a liquidation price only on an isolated position.

liquidationPrice.description: Isolated positions only: on a cross position it gives back the account's margin from public figures (d1.3).

case.time.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, the runtime's wall clock.

cases-api.list.description: GET /api/v1/cases: every stored case, newest first.

cases-api.row.description: One stored case as "What was sent" lists it, never its body. state: waiting (to be sent), sent at sentAt, held (the last check found an address at error's path; never sent), refused (by our server, error its text). sending (S3, absent on a case only the person's press sends): collecting (still open, its trigger may join it), queued (gcx sends it by itself), off (closed while automatic sending was off), skipped (past the backlog's bound); off and skipped go on the person's Send. more: occurrences of the same trigger past the day's 20 cases, kept here.

cases-api.sendBody.description: POST /api/v1/cases/{id}/send: the person's own line (500 characters), kept as written after the free-text pass.

cases-api.sent.description: The answer to a send: the stored case's id and its state (sent; waiting when our server did not answer, Send again later; held with the path where an address was found; refused with our server's text).

cases-api.usage.description: GET /api/v1/usage (S3b, d16): the install reference that stands for this gcx in every report and record, and each daily record built, newest first: its state (waiting, sent at sentAt, held: the last check found an address at error's path, refused: our server's text in error) and the record or heartbeat as it goes (pulse.schema.json).

cases-api.usageMark.description: POST /api/v1/usage/dashboard (S3b, d16.1): the Dashboard was opened. Any field is ignored: the runtime marks its own current UTC day.

cases-api.view.description: GET /api/v1/cases/{id}: the case (an order's, a bot's or the runtime's built now and written nothing; a stored one as it was stored) and, with ?timeline=<language>, its timeline.

chart-api.bar.description: One bar, opened at t. Also the data of a candles/{instrument}/{resolution} message (the forming bar).

chart-api.candles.description: Oldest first, no duplicate t. noData once the range lies beyond what the venue serves (its most recent 5,000 bars per interval).

chart-api.symbol.description: The instrument id is opaque (a HIP-3 id holds a colon). priceDecimals is 6 − szDecimals on Hyperliquid perps and 8 − szDecimals on spot, from the domain's precision rule; the chart's price scale is 10^priceDecimals.

chart-layout.content.description: What the charting library's save() returned: its own JSON object, opaque to gcx and not validated here. Drawings that gcx draws itself (order lines, position lines, planned levels) are never in it.

chart-layout.delete.description: POST /api/v1/chart/layouts/{id}/delete: an empty object. Answers an empty object, or 404 for a layout that does not exist.

name.description: Read unchanged from stored layouts, including older names over the current write limit.

indicators.description: The names of the chart's studies at save time, for the Load list. A layout without the field reads as an empty list.

pinSymbol.description: An instrument id: loading the layout switches the chart to it. Absent: the layout takes the instrument on screen.

pinInterval.description: Loading the layout switches the chart to this interval. Absent: the layout takes the interval on screen.

chart-layout.row.description: One layout as the list shows it: never its content.

chart-layout.save.description: POST /api/v1/chart/layouts/{id}: replaces the layout's meta and content. Answers `saved`; 409 with `conflict` when `baseRev` is not the current rev; 404 for a layout that does not exist.

dca-bot-create.title: DCA bot settings
dca-bot-create.description: The settings a live DCA bot runs on (decision 0016 §2, §7.2), as the reducer takes them: written by hand to mirror src/domain/dca/live.ts (DcaLiveConfig), kept equal by tests/dca/live-schema.test.ts. Each `default` is goodcryptoX's form default as ruled in 0016 §2 (what a hidden field takes); each range is the old form's. Every money, price and percentage value is a decimal string; counts and times are integers. The account, the instrument, margin and leverage, name and note join this with the create route (slice L2); the TA start's periods and signals came with the signal engine (decision 0017, slice T2). The domain refuses what a pattern cannot (validateLiveConfig): a trailing take-profit that can exit below the average, an amount of zero, the lower bound of each range.

investment.description: A3 d100: absent means quote. Quote is form metadata. Account is a percent of held account value: Approx. margin on perps (ladder margin plus the stop-loss reserve; without a stop, margin and fees plus the loss at the last averaging level), orders total on spot. Exact resolved sizing is journaled; replay never re-reads.

reinvest.description: A2 d70: grow each new cycle by all realized profit, fees and funding included; ignored with account investment

entryCondition.description: When a cycle's entry starts: at once and after each cooldown (manual), on a TA signal (ta; needs taPeriods and taSignals), on a TradingView webhook. POST /api/v1/bots refuses webhook with the named error `entry-condition-not-yet` until the Signal bot ships (release plan v4 §10). goodcryptoX's form defaulted to ta; the panel form opens on Signal too (T3), and this default stays manual: a create that omits the field must not wait on a signal nobody set.

entrySide.description: manual: buy or sell. ta: direct (the signal's side) or inverse. webhook: direct.

taPeriods.description: ta: the candle periods rated, the venue's own (Hyperliquid's fourteen); every one must agree for the bot to start (decision 0017 d8, d9). Required with ta, refused otherwise.

taSignals.description: ta: Detect signals. Buy starts at a rating above 0.1 (a score of 3 of 26), Strong Buy above 0.5 (14 of 26), Sell and Strong Sell the mirror; Buy includes Strong Buy. Required with ta, refused otherwise.

entryDistancePct.description: limit: this far from the market when the entry is made, 0 to 99; trailing: the bounce off the extreme, 0.1 to 99 (§2 row 7).

sizingMode.description: cost: amounts in the quote currency; size: in the base coin.

averaging.description: one: every level a stop-limit triggered at the previous level, one resting at a time (goodcryptoX); all: every level a resting limit at once.

postOnly.description: Averaging limits post-only; a level the market runs through fails with the averaging-error notification (RULINGS 132); Fix failed restores it.

level1Amount.description: Level 1's amount, sent as given. The panel form's Auto sends entryAmount × sizeCostMultiplier (MH 630; goodcryptoX's DEX Auto sent the entry's own amount); its Manual row starts there and follows until typed.

level1PricePct.description: Entry to averaging level 1; no multiplier. 0.01 to 99 (§2 row 13). The panel form's Auto sends avgPriceStepPct (C B2, MH 630); its Manual row starts there and follows until typed (MH 628 (a)).

sizeCostMultiplier.description: From level 2, each amount is the previous one times this. 0.01 to 10 (§2 row 14).

priceStepMultiplier.description: From level 3, each gap is the previous gap times this. 0.1 to 10 (§2 row 16).

bracketReduceOnly.description: MH366: TP/SL reduce-only preference copied at bot launch. Absent in old stored settings means true; later preference edits do not modify a running bot.

tpType.description: market: gcx watches the take-profit price and, when the last price reaches it, sends one market order for what the cycle holds; nothing rests on the exchange (goodcryptoX's Stop Market; added 2026-10-08, MH; a build before it reads it as a trailing take-profit of distance 0). limit: rests on the exchange at that price. trailing: starts trailing there and exits when the price falls back by tpTrailingDistancePct. market and limit take the same price.

tpPct.description: From the average entry price (or the entry order's price with tpFixedFromEntry). Above 0 and at most 99 with the take-profit on (§2 row 19; the form's 0 is tpEnabled false).

tpTrailingDistancePct.description: Required for a trailing take-profit; 0.1 to 99, and below tp/(1+tp) for a long, tp/(1-tp) for a short (§2 row 20).

slPct.description: Beyond the last averaging level (the entry with none). Above 0 and at most 99 with the stop-loss on (§2 row 23; the form's 0 is slEnabled false). 10 by the owner's ruling (release plan v4 A20, W21); goodcryptoX's was 15.

slLossPct.description: Added 2026-10-17 (MH 623 (c)-(f)); optional, absent: the stop is `slPct`, as before. The stop as the expected loss: a percent, above 0, of the money the bot uses (spot: the orders' value; perpetual: their margin, the value divided by the leverage; fees and the loss itself are not in it). Each cycle works out its stop for the side it opens and the account's leverage then, rounded so the loss is never more than this and within a tick of it, and keeps it for the cycle; when the loss is reached before the last averaging order, the stop goes inside the ladder and the averaging orders past it are not placed. `slPct` stays required: the distance a build before this one runs on, and what a cycle uses when the leverage could not be read. Only with slEnabled.

repeatOnTp.description: A new cycle after a take-profit, a Close pos. or any close that is not the stop-loss.

cooldownMs.description: The wait between cycles, in milliseconds: the form's menu offers none, 5 min, 30 min, 1 hour, 6 hours and 1 day; any other whole length is a custom one (added 2026-10-17, MH 708; before, only those six were accepted).

closeOnStop.description: Stop closes the position at market.

wholePosition.description: Only this bot trades this pair (was "Only gcx trades this coin"; MH 2026-10-05 line 33, 2026-10-06 rules 321 and 322; decision 0028 d21): a comparison only, never a size. On, a difference between the exchange's position on the coin and the bot's count on two reads gcx can trust waits for the person (red), and something else seen trading the pair (a fill or an order resting at the exchange that is not this bot's) is a notice (yellow); on spot only fewer coins than the bot counts differ. "Exchange is right" then counts every fill on the pair as this bot's. Off: nothing is raised. On only for the single bot on a pair: a bot created beside another that is not done is made with it off, and those with it on turn it off. Changed at once by modify. The take-profit, the stop-loss and every close sell only what the bot bought, on or off. Required on every create; the form starts ticked (unticked on perpetuals with a position open on the coin).

startAt.description: When to start, ms since the epoch.

endAt.description: When to stop, ms since the epoch.

atEnd.description: At the end time: finish the cycle; exit now (close); stop and keep the position.

dca-bot-create.decimal.description: A plain unsigned decimal string, never a JSON number.

dca-bot-create.mult10.description: A decimal string from 0 to 10, the old form's top for a multiplier (AF:1825-1840); the lower bound is the domain's.

dca-bot-create.pct99.description: A decimal string from 0 to 99, the old form's top for every percentage (AF:1809-1865); the lower bound of each field is the domain's (validateLiveConfig).

deviceId.description: 16 random bytes, base64url, minted at the pairing; the last 16 bytes of its passkey's user handle.

name.description: The browser and the system at the pairing ("Safari on iPhone"), renamed by the person.

canTrade.description: The switch: true Can trade (everything the person can do at the computer), false Read-only (reads only; every write 403). A device starts at Can trade (ruling 3).

lastUsedAt.description: The last sign-in or request, written at most once a minute; null before the first.

machine.description: Added 2026-10-18 (0014, ruling 17): the name of the machine goodcryptoX runs on, its network name as the passkey sheet shows it, without a trailing ".local" ("MacBook-Pro-3"). The panel's first row is this computer under it; an older runtime leaves it out, an empty one reads as absent.

device.pair.description: The answer to POST /api/v1/devices/pair: the link, which holds the pairing code in its fragment (it reaches no server), and when it stops working. The panel draws its QR from the link.

text.description: Optional: the sentence a person reads. A 503 `starting` while a start-up check holds (the computer's clock more than 5 s off the exchange's, the API wallet absent or expired, the exchange unreadable) carries that check's own sentence, with what to change.

exits-command.attach.description: Attach a take-profit and stop-loss. On a position: one per account and coin, sized from the position and following it as it changes (reduce-only as `bracket.reduceOnly` says, default true whatever Settings say, MH 520; existing exits retain it); the answer `{id}` names the exits (`x1`, ...). On an order of gcx's: open, partly filled or filled, not a bot's, not an exit; sized from what it filled; the exits take the order's id.

order.description: The order's id, as the orders topic gives it.

exits-command.cancel.description: End every take-profit and stop-loss of these exits that is still working.

exits-command.edit.description: Edit TP/SL: the whole block again. Targets are positional: target i of the block is take-profit i, filled ones included, in their place; a take-profit or stop-loss that was cancelled has left the block and is never made again unless sent as a new one. A filled target is never sent again; the rest are re-sized from what is still held. `bracket.reduceOnly` absent: an order's TP/SL keep what they have; sent: it wins; a position's keep the choice made at attach (MH 520).

exits-command.overrides.description: Keys of the warnings the caller sends anyway: the order form's overridable warnings and the two of a DCA bot on the coin (RULINGS 65). Errors cannot be overridden.

exits-command.requestId.description: Caller-minted id (the panel uses a UUID); the runtime answers the same request once.

investment.description: A3 d100: absent means quote. Quote is form metadata. Account is a percent of held account value: Approx. margin on perps (orders margin plus the stop-loss reserve; Grid without a stop reserves to the far band edge, DCA without a stop reserves the loss at the last averaging level plus margin and fees), orders total on spot. Exact resolved sizing is journaled; replay never re-reads.

distance.description: Trailing exit distance in percent. Required and positive for trailing-stop exits.

oneOf.description: Catalogue Q14: bot stops or errors; TP and SL fills; entry and averaging fills from level fromLevel (0 = all).

profitInCoin.description: Spot only: closing orders recover the opening quote and both fees, retaining the profit in coin.

followUp.description: Follow the price up (0040 a1 d34). Absent means off: a grid stored without it never moves. Supported with quote or coin sizing.

followDown.description: Follow the price down (0040 a1 d34). Absent means off. Supported with quote or coin sizing.

useHeld.description: Spot: the start uses the free coins of the pair the account holds and buys only the rest (0040 a1 d33).

upTo.description: The highest price the band moves to; null or absent is no limit (0040 a1 d37).

downTo.description: The lowest price the band moves to; null or absent is no limit (0040 a1 d37).

grid-bot-create.properties.distance.description: Trailing exit distance in percent. Required and positive for trailing-stop exits.

grid-bot-create.properties.downTo.description: The lowest price the band moves to; null or absent is no limit (0040 a1 d37).

grid-profitability.title: Grid profitability buckets
grid-profitability.description: G12 producer for G11: full snapshot without profitAfter; replacement values for changed hours/days with it. Funding is already inside realized. UTC hour starts for the newest 30 days, UTC day starts before.

current.description: A4 Current at this bucket’s latest step, never a running maximum.

heldArea.description: Incremental quote × ms since the preceding recorded bucket update, accumulated within this bucket; never add this replacement twice.

grid-rule.title: Exact Grid level rule
grid-rule.description: 0040 v3 d4. The typed range becomes one exact linear step or logarithmic ratio at 34 digits. Buttons change only count or i0. Prices are decimal strings; indices and counts are integers. Venue-tick rounding and duplicate merging happen when cells are derived, never when the rule is saved.

instrument-display.title: Catalogue instrument display
instrument-display.description: MH674: additive display metadata beside instrumentId. Omitted by older runtimes; readers keep the former id fallback until the name is served. Never a command identifier.

instrument-row.title: Instrument row
instrument-row.description: One instrument as GET /api/v1/instruments?venue serves it: the domain Instrument record (its trading rules) as strings, plus display fields and the 24-hour stats. The whole response is $defs/list, with a version so the panel does not refetch on every open. Mirrors src/panel/model/instruments.ts (InstrumentRow, InstrumentList). See decision 0007 part 3 decision 9.

id.description: The venue's instrument id, with the dex prefix on HIP-3 (xyz:SPCX).

quote.description: The quote asset; on perps the settlement asset of the notional.

szDecimals.description: Sizes are floored to 10^-szDecimals (a count, not money).

minNotional.description: Minimum order value in quote; "0" = none.

marginModes.description: ["isolated"] on an isolated-only instrument; [] on spot.

limitBandPct.description: Added 2026-10-04 (ruling 158): the exchange refuses a limit order priced further than this percent from its reference price (Hyperliquid perpetuals: 80; venue-caps.schema.json limitBandPct). The DCA form warns of a planned order beyond it, less a 1 % cushion, before Launch; the runtime refuses such a bot. Absent: no bound (spot).

priceRule.description: A price has at most sigFigs significant figures and maxDecimals decimals; an integer is always valid (Hyperliquid: 5 and 6 - szDecimals).

rungs.description: The order book's aggregation rungs (0007 part 1).

change24h.description: 24-hour Hyperliquid mark-price change versus prevDayPx, percent; used by the selector column, sorts and Gainers/Losers (MH ruling 373)

caps.description: What the venue offers the form. The first order type is the venue's default, used when a carried type is not offered.

spot.description: Spot orders can be sent (true under `gcx run` since E15). When false, the form still shows Buy and Sell on a spot market and the runtime refuses the order.

spotListed.description: Spot markets are listed: the selector's Spot tab, their chart, book and trades. Optional; when absent it is the value of `spot`. Kept for compatibility; under `gcx run` it equals `spot`.

maxTimeInForce.description: The venue's longest time in force, milliseconds.

lists-api.allAnswer.description: Cancel all's, Stop all's and Close all's answer: what was cancelled, stopped or closed (each order's, bot's or position's own command accepted) and what was refused, with its sentence. count 0 and ids [] when the filter matched nothing: nothing was done.

count.description: How many were cancelled, stopped or closed: ids' length.

code.description: Names the refusal where one is known: `bot-order` (a bot's own order: its bot's Stop cancels it) or `bot-position` (a position a running bot holds: the bot's Close pos. or Stop closes it; added 2026-10-09) or `below-minimum` (Close all's part of a position bots hold part of is under the exchange's minimum order value, `text` names it; added 2026-10-09). Absent for a refusal with no code, and from a runtime older than this field; a client says the code in its own language and shows `text` for one it does not know. Added 2026-10-05.

bots.description: Close all with bots stop: each bot whose Stop (or a stopped one's Force close) was accepted. Absent otherwise, and from a runtime older than this field. Added 2026-10-09.

lists-api.botCommand.description: POST /api/v1/bots/{id}/command with decision 0016 §7.1's command kinds (src/domain/dca/live.ts BotCommand, plus mismatch and notify, which the runtime keeps). The runtime deduplicates on requestId. Nothing is edited by writing a row.

oneOf.description: keep (0028 d4): "Bot is right" on a red item, "Accept" on the yellow notice: nothing sent, "Only this bot trades this pair" turned off; a person's only.

from.description: The scope of the fields that are not goodcryptoX's five: from the next cycle, the only scope in V1 (V1.1 adds this-cycle). Optional and ignored in a request; the runtime journals it when a field waits for the next cycle (a cycle open at the press, 0016 Amendment 7), and an older runtime whenever such a field was present.

oneOf.description: Added with 0016 Amendment 9: the Run row's and the stop row's change that removes a value, the only command that sets or moves the end. `fields` sets, `clear` removes: maxCycles (Run until stopped), endAt with its atEnd (no end), slLossPct (the stop back to its distance, slPct, from the next cycle while a cycle is open; a later modify setting slLossPct cancels it); nothing is both set and removed. The end applies at once and moves its timer; days count from the bot's real start. Refused 422 like modify, and when maxCycles is below the cycles done or endAt has passed. An older runtime ignores the row.

from.description: As modify's: journaled when a set or removed field waits for the next cycle.

oneOf.description: 0016 Amendment 2: the person's choice on a bot whose position differs from the exchange's (a person's only; a key is refused 403). `exchange`: the exchange's signed size the person saw; the runtime reads the exchange again at the press and asks again (409 with the new figures) when it changed. `restore` also carries the size the person confirmed (the difference), and `anyway` once ruling 141's warning was passed.

lists-api.cancelAllBody.description: POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all (MH 2026-10-05: "Cancel all / Stop all, applied to whatever is filtered in the list"; "also in the API and MCP, with filters"): every open order the filter matches, as the Open orders list shows them (src/domain/lists/filter.ts), each cancelled as its own cancel would be (one request per order, under requestId/<order id>), orders placed outside gcx included when they match. A bot's order is never cancelled here: it is listed in refused ("This order is a bot's: stop the bot to cancel its orders."), as its row has no Cancel; the bot's Stop cancels it. Every filter field is optional; without one, every order the caller may see: a person's every open order, a trading key's only the orders it placed. Answers allAnswer.

sourceId.description: The account (the list's scope: this exchange).

instrumentId.description: The pair (the list's scope: this pair).

type.description: The list's type filter: a family of order types.

source.description: Placed by gcx, or outside it.

children.description: Legacy child-order filter, still accepted by the API. The panel no longer exposes a Child orders toggle. Absent: true.

lists-api.cancelBody.description: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel from a list row. The runtime deduplicates on requestId; the row says 'cancel requested' until the order is terminal.

lists-api.closeAllBody.description: POST /api/v1/positions/close-all (MH 2026-10-09, the third of Cancel all and Stop all): every position the filter matches, as the Positions list shows them, read from the exchange now, each closed as its own Close would be (a reduce-only market order for the whole position as the exchange reports it, under requestId/<account id>:<instrument>). Every filter field is optional; without one, every position the caller may see: a person's every account's, a trading key's only the accounts ticked for it (a key with no limits: 422 key.noLimits). A bot's part of a position (a running bot's, or a bot's stopped without closing that still holds it) is never sold from under it (ruling 397, MH 2026-10-09): with bots keep it is left, listed in refused with the code bot-position, and the rest of that position (a mixed one, partly the person's) is closed as a reduce-only Close of the position as gcx reads it at the send less what the bots hold, rounded down to the size step, or refused with the code below-minimum when that part is under the exchange's minimum order value; with bots stop the person's part closes the same way, then each bot is stopped with its position closed (a stopped one force-closed), a trading key's only the bots it created. An account whose positions could not be read is listed in refused under its account id; nothing is closed there. A position row's own Close on a bot's position sends this with the row's account and pair (ruling 401 a). Answers allAnswer.

sourceId.description: The account (the list's scope: this exchange).

instrumentId.description: The pair (the list's scope: this pair).

side.description: buy: long positions; sell: short positions.

bots.description: What to do with a bot's part of a position: keep (the bots' parts stay, the bots keep running) or stop (each bot closes its position and ends). Absent: keep. Added 2026-10-09.

lists-api.correction.description: Added with 0028 d23.4 (stream 2): one correction row of the cycle, what the fills did not reach after Exchange is right (or the rest below the minimum left to the person): the cycle's size and cost before and after, nothing realized (pnl 0), the price used (the exchange's entry, or the bot's average; never a last price), the bracket of the difference, the cause, and reach: the oldest time the venue's history served when it did not reach the cycle's start.

lists-api.dcaDetails.description: GET /api/v1/bots/{id}?iteration=n: the details object, with its own seq (decision 0016 §8.2; roadmap B9). `planned` and `activity` are one iteration's (the current one unless asked); `cycles` every started cycle's realized PnL, the one under way included, oldest first (B68).

modifiedByPerson.description: An accepted personal Modify after creation, projected incrementally; absent means no known personal modification

chartOrders.description: Optional recorded facts: snapshot replaces; delta updates only named orders in this exact bot/cycle. Canonical activity stays complete.

chartCycle.description: Optional selected-cycle recorded facts for chart properties. iteration equals this details iteration; bot remains the current overview and permissions source. Older runtimes omit this field.

planned.description: The iteration's orders as planned: the entry at its average, each averaging level with its status, the stop-loss and the take-profit.

status.description: An averaging level's: below the exchange's minimum, not sent (0016 d4); waiting for its trigger; sent; filled; failed (Fix failed restores it); cancelled.

funding.description: The iteration's funding payments, oldest first: the bot's share of each hourly payment on its coin, paid negative, received positive, at the venue's hour. Listed among `activity` by time as "Funding received" / "Funding paid"; display only, the bot's funding figure already is their sum. Absent while the iteration has none.

Added 2026-10-14 (MH 8956 comment 190 b): the funding the cycle booked (the bot's share, paid negative); absent while it booked none. The cycle's realised PnL including funding (0007 amendment 8) is realized + funding. The previous build ignores it.

fundingDays.description: Added 2026-10-26 (MH item 26, the Profitability chart books funding in the week it was paid): `funding` summed by UTC day, oldest first, each at the time of that day's last payment; their sum is `funding`. Absent while the cycle has no payments, and from an older runtime: the chart then books `funding` at `closedAt`. The previous build ignores it.

invested.description: C91: the closed cycle’s recorded entry cost plus levels cost, projected from the held iteration alongside realized and funding. Optional for older runtimes; not a timestamped history of the running cycle’s capital.

heldPeak.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 736 (4)), on a closed cycle beside `invested`: the most the bot had on the exchange (its position at entry prices and its entry and averaging orders resting there, as the row's `investedPeak` counts it) while this was its current cycle. The chart's Max reached. Absent while it had nothing there, and from an older runtime: the chart then takes `invested`. The previous build ignores it.

heldArea.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 736 (4)), on a closed cycle beside `invested`: the same figure summed over the time it was the current cycle, in quote × milliseconds (the cycles' sum over the running time is the row's `investedAverage`). The chart's Average. Absent as `heldPeak`: the chart then takes `invested` over the time since the previous close. The previous build ignores it.

closedAt.description: Added 2026-10-09 (RULINGS 370 a; the Returns chart's daily bars): when the cycle closed, ms since the epoch: the exchange's time of the latest exit fill (take-profit, stop-loss, close) or liquidation fill of the cycle; a cycle recorded before 0016 amendment 5: when gcx recorded it. Derived from the book, not stored. Absent on the cycle under way and on one that closed without an exit fill. The previous build ignores it.

beside.description: Q8: the bots' size on this coin and the exchange's, while they differ and the person has not said they know why.

attention.description: Added 2026-10-05 (decision 0016 Amendment 2 §5, §6): the bot's position differs from the exchange's and the item is open (the bot paused its new orders until the person chooses). bot: the bot's own count, signed; exchange: the exchange's position (on spot the holding), signed, as confirmed on two trusted reads; since: the last agreement; opened: when the item opened; cause: the likely one (liquidation, gcx: a person's order in gcx, outside: a trade not placed by gcx, none: no trade seen); fills: the account's fills on the coin since the last agreement that are not a bot's, newest first; restoring: a restore of the coin is out, only Stop is offered. Absent when nothing differs and on a done bot. Cause refused (added 2026-10-05, RULINGS 218 b): on spot the exchange refused the bot's sale of the rest of its exit for want of coins; the item opened on that refusal, so exchange is absent until a read gives it, and the choices finish the exit (the account's coins counted and sold; the rest sent once more).

items.description: Added with 0028 d18 (stream 2): the bot's open items in d17's order (what leaves a position unprotected first; then the count; then other stuck orders; then what blocks a start; then the yellow notice; Retry order last), beside the older `attention`. Absent while none.

corrections.description: Added with 0028 d23.4 (stream 2): the iteration's correction rows, oldest first; the trades list shows each as one row Correction. Absent while none.

released.description: Added 2026-10-09 (ruling 406 b): when the bot, stopped without closing, let go of the iteration's part because a fresh read showed the account flat on the coin (sold outside gcx), ms since the epoch; the activity shows it as one row. Absent before, and for a bot that never did.

held.description: The bot's sends held for the person (RULINGS 96).

why.description: Added in E11: maintenance, held while the exchange was in maintenance; it goes by itself when the maintenance ends (0013 amendment 3).

pending.description: Settings changed while a cycle runs, not yet in force (0016 Amendment 1 B46; the bot's `next`): the details show them with "applies from the next cycle". Absent when none wait. `clear` added with 0016 Amendment 9: the settings removed from the next cycle (today slLossPct, the stop back to its distance), absent when none; `settings` may then be empty.

lists-api.fundingRows.description: GET /api/v1/funding?sourceId=&instrumentId=: every hourly funding payment gcx journaled on a coin of an account, oldest first, the rows of a position's details. `usdc` received positive, paid negative. Missed payments are added after successful fill and funding recovery from the account tracking boundary. `bots`: what each bot on the coin was charged of the payment, by what it held that hour; the rest is the person's.

time.description: The venue's hour of the payment.

modifiedByPerson.description: An accepted personal Modify after creation, projected incrementally; absent means no known personal modification

children.description: The grid's open orders the chart draws, from the open index; ended children use indexed viewport history

profitAfter.description: Opaque grid-bound revision cursor. Omit on a details page's first read; pass back for changed buckets only.

profitabilityRemoved.description: Delete these old hour timestamps before upserting profitability. A day bucket may replace an hour at the same timestamp.

lists-api.historyPage.description: GET /api/v1/history?…&cursor: terminal orders by (closedAt, id), newest first, with the list's filter applied by the same predicate the panel uses. Defaults to manual orders across all pairs and accounts; an explicit botId retains access to that bot’s terminal orders. No query or row field is removed. Never sorted by a money column.

order.description: Only for order=changedAt: confirms indexed same-account/pair marker history sorted by the factual last-change timestamp, the person's rows, or with botId that bot's (MH 285); older servers omit it and ignore botId in this mode.

lists-api.item.description: Added with 0028 d11, d18 (stream 2): one open item, whatever gcx cannot settle by itself and waits for a person's answer, derived from the bot's or the order's records (src/domain/repair/items.ts), never stored. The runtime topic's `attention` rows and GET /api/v1/bots/{id} carry the same. id: `<bot>:<cause>` or `<orderId>:order`; key: `<id>:<episode>`, the handle of Telegram's message, of POST /api/v1/attention/silence and of a new episode (a refusal of the answer's act opens a new one); cause: the catalogue's code (0028 d15); level: red holds (the bot's new risk, d3), yellow is the notice, which holds nothing (RULINGS 319 a); holds: new-risk, nothing, or order (only that order waits); answers: the codes of the existing commands, in order (adopt Exchange is right, keep Bot is right on red and Accept on yellow, restore Retry of a refused sale, match Make the exchange match the bot, free Cancel that order, retry Retry, close Close position, cancel Cancel order, stop Stop bot, level Retry order, renew and limits open Settings, accept-venue older journals); since: the episode's time; acting: an answer's act is out (match); orderId: the order it is about; words: the exchange's own words; preview (GET /api/v1/bots/{id} only, on the items Exchange is right answers, d22.8, RULINGS 330 a): what the bot will count after Exchange is right, figured as the press figures it from the venue's history and a read of the exchange, read again when the item shows a new exchange figure (size and cost after the correction, what the fills found realize, the correction's size, and the fills at the venue's time), or failed: they could not be read and gcx reads them again every minute and at the press. A newer cause or answer may appear; a reader shows what it knows.

facts.description: Added with 0028 d15, d26 (repair-item-facts): what the item shows beside it and the records give. refused-held (C2h): `orders`, the person's resting sells on the pair that hold the coins the bot's sale needs (the venue's id, or a gcx order's own); foreign (the yellow notice): `fills`, the trades by others since the last agreement (the venue's time), and `orders`, the resting orders by others. Absent on every other item.

correction.description: Added with RULINGS 330 a: the size the correction moves the count by, for what the fills do not reach (0 for none); `size` and `cost` are the cycle after it.

lists-api.listPage.description: C64 explicit whole-store display read. Held names feed exactly the same bulk predicate. No query runs on a live-row event. Cursor boundaries retain comparison facts rather than promising a frozen live snapshot.

recentForcedCloses.description: Optional recent forced-close facts; a supplied empty array clears prior facts. Display-only, excluded from all close/increase commands and live balances.

waitingFor.description: Optional pending first-read account IDs for venue-backed lists. Omitted for known data and local Bots/History owners; absence does not authorize client metadata reconstruction.

nextCursor.description: Present when another page exists; authoritative for newest-first History, which does not count the whole query.
