total.description: Matching-row count; a visited-match lower bound for default newest-first History pages, an exact count for explicitly requested other sorts.

lists-api.modifyFields.description: Any setting of dca-bot-create.schema.json but the entry condition and the end time (0016 Amendment 1 B46; the TA periods and signals added by 0016 Amendment 7, MH 669: a TA bot's only, 422 on another; startAt and atEnd added by its d9, MH 709 (a), 710 (a): startAt only while the bot waits for its start, 422 otherwise, its start timer moved to the new time; atEnd, what happens when the days end, at once). goodcryptoX's five (closeOnStop, repeatOnTp, repeatOnSl, tpFixedFromEntry, cooldownMs; 0016 d16; a cooldown changed during the cooldown counts from its start), wholePosition ("Only this bot trades this pair", 0028 d21.6: on is refused while another bot that is not done trades the pair; off closes the bot's open count item and yellow notice) and the bot's name and note (B65, the limits of the create's; also on a stopped bot) apply at once; every other field at once while no cycle is open (waiting to start, for its signal, in its cooldown, closing, or held before its entry is sent; the details serve the current cycle's chartCycle.open) and from the next cycle while one is: the open cycle keeps its ladder and exits. The answer's applied says which. The runtime validates the settings the next cycle will run on as at creation (422 with the reason).

lists-api.notify.description: Catalogue Q14: bot stops or errors; TP and SL fills; entry and averaging fills from level fromLevel (0 = all).

lists-api.orderDetails.description: GET /api/v1/orders/{id}: the details object, with its own seq; re-read when the order's row changes.

chart.description: Only with chartAfter: cold/reset snapshot or newly appended facts. Cursor binds ledger and target, never timestamp.

entry.description: The levels' base: a position's entry; an order's fills' average once its bracket is armed (added 2026-10-18; absent before the full fill, when the levels follow the anchor).

bracket.description: Existing canonical bracket spec and leg membership/state, copied read-only; never reconstructed from rendered prices.

openPrice.description: The market price when the order was created.

feeRates.description: Added 2026-10-28 (0040 amendment 6): on a grid order, the account's fee rates as the bot's details serve them (`maker`, `taker` fractions, `at` the read's time or null for the venue's base rates); a trailing exit's Price improvement compares with a limit at the maker rate. Absent on other orders and from older runtimes.

platformFee.description: Deprecated 2026-10-17 (0004 amendment note): never set by any runtime; the order row's `builderFee` carries the platform fee. To be removed in a later release.

parent.description: 0034: derived from the row’s botId or known order parentId. Absent means no known parent order or bot; a position exit has none here.

parentRow.description: 0034: optional canonical parent order row. Omitted by older runtimes or when the parent is absent; then the card uses only a held parent row.

chartOrders.description: Optional recorded child facts, keyed by actual current child/rest ID. Parent snapshot replaces; parent delta updates only named child groups with their own snapshot/delta marker.

children.description: Every served child/rest row; empty means none.

id.description: Stable admitted display fact ID; not a tradable order ID.

triggerPrice.description: Optional on modified facts: the preceding admitted stop/trigger, independent of the old limit price.

activationPrice.description: Optional on modified trail facts: preceding admitted activation. Null means known absent; older omitted facts do not authorize reconstructed marks.

fired.description: Optional on modified facts: the preceding admitted triggered state. False is positively not yet triggered; older omission is unknown, never inferred by comparing venue and admission times.

trailPhase.description: Optional on modified trail facts: the preceding admitted phase, not today's row phase.

trailStartedAt.description: Optional on modified facts: the preceding revision’s admitted trailing activation timestamp. Never copied from a later activation or inferred when absent.

trailStartedPointId.description: Optional on modified facts: the preceding revision’s admitted activation point id, distinguishing equal-timestamp revisions. Never copied from a later activation.

improveOnlyPrice.description: Optional on modified facts: the preceding admitted improve-only activation guide, distinct from command Start after trailing begins. Absence remains unknown, never reconstructed from today's row.

improveOnly.description: Optional on modified trail facts: the preceding admitted improve-only setting, for its activation label.

trail.description: Trailing orders once the trail started: the engine's journaled stop history, oldest first (first = initial trigger, last = current), and the best price since the start (decision 0005 §1.3a). The chart draws it as a step path.

lists-api.orderDetails.properties.chart.description: Only with chartAfter: cold/reset snapshot or newly appended facts. Cursor binds ledger and target, never timestamp.

lists-api.resendBody.description: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/resend (the docs judge's G1): a manual order in repair (its row's status unknown, with why) sent again, the order as it stands (0013 amendment 1's Re-place; an unanswered cancel of it is sent again instead). Journaled with the request before anything is sent; the same request answers the same. Answers {accepted: true}; 422 {rejected, text} when the order is no longer in repair, while a send of it has no answer yet, for a missed order (it takes execute-now or place-back), or for a bot's order; 503 when an order that adds risk cannot be sent now. The runtime deduplicates on requestId, per order and per action. Added 2026-10-04.

lists-api.sendNowBody.description: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/send-now (the docs judge's G2; 0013 ruling 1): a send gcx holds for the person (its row's held says why) sent now, once. The request is journaled before the send; the same request answers the same. Answers {accepted: true}; 422 {rejected, text} when nothing of the order is held, when its position changed while it waited (cancel it and place it again), or for a bot's order; 503 when an order that adds risk cannot be sent now (Hyperliquid's maintenance, a full disk, gcx starting or stopping). The runtime deduplicates on requestId, per order and per action. Added 2026-10-04.

lists-api.stopAllBody.description: POST /api/v1/bots/stop-all (MH 2026-10-05): every bot not done that the filter matches, as the Bots list shows them, each stopped as its own Stop would be (bot command stop, under requestId/<bot id>; a stopped bot cancels its own orders and closes per its close-on-stop setting). Every filter field is optional; without one, every bot the caller may see: a person's every bot, a trading key's only the bots it created. Answers allAnswer.

side.description: buy: long bots; sell: short bots.

notify-api.empty.description: The body of POST /api/v1/notify/telegram/pair, /start, /recheck and /disconnect: nothing.

notify-api.linked.description: POST /api/v1/notify/telegram/token: the bot Telegram accepted. 422 {error, code} when it refused the token or did not answer: `code` is `token-invalid` (Telegram refused it), `unknown` (Telegram did not answer) or `not-saved` (the token could not be kept where gcx runs); `error` is the English sentence, `code` is what the panel words.

notify-api.paired.description: POST /api/v1/notify/telegram/pair: Telegram's create link to open (d11 (a)). 422 {error, code} when one touch is not available: `code` is `one-touch`.

notify-api.sample.description: The body of POST /api/v1/dev/telegram/send (ruling 82, the Internal build only): the template to send with demo data, one of the `template` values of GET /api/v1/dev/telegram/samples.

notify-api.samples.description: GET /api/v1/dev/telegram/samples (ruling 82, the Internal build only; 404 on every other tier): every message with demo data, its title and first line in the person's language, in the order of the three groups (manual: Orders, bots: Bots, account: Account).

line.description: The message's first line of text under its title; titles alone repeat, title and line do not.

notify-api.sent.description: POST /api/v1/dev/telegram/send: the sample went into the outbox, to its topic. 422 {error, code} when no chat is linked: `code` is `not-linked`; 404 for an unknown template or on a tier other than Internal.

notify-api.startLink.description: POST /api/v1/notify/telegram/start: "Open your bot": https://t.me/<bot>?start=<nonce>, the nonce single-use for 10 minutes (only its hash is kept). 404 when no bot is kept.

notify-api.state.description: GET /api/v1/notify/telegram, and the answer of POST /recheck: the bot, whether a chat is bound, the link's state, the topics, the outbox's counts and a one-touch set-up in progress.

bot.description: The bot's @username; null when none is kept.

bound.description: A chat was bound by /start <nonce> and messages go to it.

state.description: blocked: the owner blocked the bot, sending waits until they write to it; token-invalid: Telegram refused the token; polling-stopped: another copy of the runtime reads this bot (Re-check restarts it).

topics.description: Messages go to the three topics (Orders, Bots, Account); false: one chat.

dropped.description: Messages given up, each with its reason (the health line).

pairing.description: The one-touch set-up's state (telegram-relay.schema.json); null where it is not available.

notify-api.token.description: POST /api/v1/notify/telegram/token: the token BotFather gave (d11 (b)). Telegram must accept it (getMe) before it is kept, in the file telegram.token in the data folder, readable by its owner only; it is never answered, logged or stored anywhere else.

notify-settings.properties.notifyBotDefa.description: Settings › Alerts › For new bots (rulings 46; 0009 d2): the notification switches a DCA bot gets when it is created, which the form shows and the person may change for that bot. Written whole. stops: bot stops or errors; tpSl: take-profit and stop-loss fills; fills: entry and averaging fills; fromLevel: those fills from this level on (0 is the entry order).

notify-settings.properties.notifyManual.description: Settings › Alerts › Manual orders placed from gcx (rulings 46): the Telegram message of a manual order's fill and of its trigger or trailing start. Off: those messages are not sent. A manual order's repair and alerts are always sent.

notify-settings.properties.notifyOutside.description: Settings › Alerts › Orders placed outside gcx (rulings 46): a fill of an order placed outside gcx (the venue's own app or another tool) on a gcx account sends "fill (external)". Off: it does not. Seen while the account's stream is open.

notify-settings.properties.telegramButto.description: Shortcut buttons under gcx's Telegram messages (0009 Amendment 1): Stop bot, Close position, Retry, Retry order, Relaunch, the three TP/SL shortcuts. Off: new messages carry the panel link only, and a press on an older message answers "Shortcut buttons are off in Settings" and does nothing.

notify-settings.properties.telegramConfi.description: "Ask before a Telegram shortcut acts": the first press shows what the button will do, with Confirm and Cancel, for one minute; off, the first press acts. One switch for every button. A guard against a mistaken tap, not against another person.

order-command.title: Order command
order-command.description: What the panel and the agent surface send to place an order (POST /api/v1/orders). Every number is a decimal string, never a JSON number. One variant per order type; a field of another type is refused. The runtime dedups on requestId and re-validates with its own tick, balances, position and leverage. Mirrors src/domain/orders/command.ts (OrderCommand). See decisions 0004 §1 and 0007 part 3 decision 4, and docs/reference/orders/validation.md.

requestId.description: Caller-minted id (the panel uses a UUID); the runtime makes one order per id.

sourceId.description: The source the order is for: a venue account or a wallet, never the caller

instrumentId.description: The instrument id, e.g. BTC or xyz:SPCX.

type.description: The order type; each variant below fixes it and allows only that type's fields.

overrides.description: Keys of the warnings the user chose to send anyway. Only overridable warnings can be listed; errors cannot be overridden. A trading key's order is sent with its warnings whatever it lists here (RULINGS 75).

order-command.bracket.description: Take-profit targets and one stop-loss attached to the order, placed on its fills. Every combination is valid here, including a limit take-profit with a stop-loss, by hand or from the DCA bot, on perps and on spot (ruling 381 b); on spot gcx's own stop-loss cancels the resting take-profit first and sells once the exchange confirmed the cancel (ruling 296 c).

reduceOnly.description: The take-profit and stop-loss only reduce the position (perpetuals). Default true: absent, the take-profit and stop-loss are reduce-only, whatever Settings › Trading says (MH 520); a received value is honoured. Spot has no reduce-only.

timeInForce.description: Added 2026-10-05 (MH, audit list 24): the take-profit and stop-loss's own time in force, one for both, counted from the order's full fill (on a position, from when they are set); at its end every one still open is cancelled, with one notice. Absent with no cancelAt: one year (31536000000 ms) for new API/MCP submissions, independent of panel Settings (MH481). Old journal rows retain no expiry. An older build ignores it.

cancelAt.description: C79 B2/B4: cancel both TP/SL legs at this UTC moment, not with timeInForce. MH480, MH484 (500 (1)): not before the entry's expiry and (a market or gc-market entry expires at its send; on a position or an order already filled, counted from acceptance): before the entry's expiry is HTTP 400, equality accepted; more than one year after it is the overridable warning trade.bracket.msgExpiryTooLong (HTTP 422 until named in overrides). A late full fill retains this end; the old journal failure path expires elapsed exits without placing. Older readers ignore this field and do not support absolute TP/SL expiry.

order-command.cancelAt.description: Added in E16 (0011 d14): cancel the order if still open at this moment; not with timeInForce. The runtime journals it as the time in force from the order's send. Absent (and no timeInForce): one year for new API/MCP submissions, independent of panel Settings. Old journal rows retain no expiry.

order-command.close.description: The exit order: market, reduce-only, sized by the runtime from the position. No side and no size.

order-command.exitTimeInForce.description: MH484: above zero and at most one year, 31536000000 milliseconds; over the limit is HTTP 400 with the house limit message, never silently cut.

order-command.gc-market.description: Market, cancelled if not filled within the venue's wait (legacy GC-Market). On an Ioc venue such as Hyperliquid it behaves as market.

order-command.instant.description: A moment, in milliseconds since the epoch (UTC), as a string.

order-command.levelMode.description: percent or quoted: a distance from the parent's price; price: an absolute level.

order-command.millis.description: A duration in milliseconds, as a string.

order-command.oneTime.description: A moment or a duration, never both (0011 d14).

sizeUnit.description: base: the base asset; quote: the quote asset (on perps the notional, never the margin). A quote size is converted to base by the engine and floored to the size step; on spot a market buy's at the ask plus the 1 % entry cap, its limit at the exchange, so it never costs more than the amount.

reduceOnly.description: Only reduce the position. On a perpetual an order whose side and size close the position exactly, as gcx reads it when the order arrives, is sent reduce-only without it too, and gets no minimum-order-value warning (since 2026-10-05). On spot, which has no position, it is dropped and the order sent without it (since 2026-10-05; refused before).

delay.description: Timed placement: send after this long.

sendAt.description: Added in E16 (0011 d14): send at this moment; not with delay. The runtime journals it as the delay from its receipt; a moment not ahead of the runtime's clock is refused. Absent (and no delay): sent now.

expected.description: Deprecated (MH 2026-10-05): accepted and ignored. The order goes at the leverage and margin mode the exchange has when it is sent; set them with POST /api/v1/leverage. Until 2026-10-05 an order was refused when this differed from the exchange's.

mode.description: loss: value is the expected loss in quote.

follow.description: Follow TPs: move to break-even at the first target, or to the previous target at each. Off when absent.

price.description: The limit price sent when the trigger fires.

postOnly.description: The limit sent at the trigger rests post-only (the DCA bot's averaging orders).

triggerTimeout.description: After the first crossing, wait this long and fire only if the price is still across.

value.description: Percent, quote distance or price, per mode.

share.description: Percent of the parent's filled size this target closes.

order-command.timeInForce.description: Resting orders: cancel if still open this long after placement; above zero (zero is refused, HTTP 400). Absent with no cancelAt: one year (31536000000 ms), the API/MCP product default, independent of panel Settings (MH481).

minProfit.description: Percent; activation waits until this profit (improve-only).

trailStart.description: Trailing starts when the price reaches this level; absent: from placement.

order-row.title: Order row
order-row.description: One order as the `orders` topic, the History pages and the details carry it. Money is a decimal string. `status` is the lifecycle only; 'partially filled' is derived from `filled`. Mirrors src/panel/model/frames.ts (OrderRow). See decision 0007 part 2 §9.1.

closedBy.description: A4: paired filled order ids, all partners; never inferred by a page read.

closed.description: A4: paired filled order ids, all partners; never inferred by a page read.

seq.description: The ledger event id of the row's last change. A row applies only if its seq is newer than the one held.

requestId.description: The form's command id, until the row replaces the form's pending state.

removed.description: Added 2026-10-10 (0003b amendment 3 d1, rulings 339 and 413.3): the row's account is being removed from gcx or was removed with its trading history kept; the row takes no action. Absent otherwise.

account.description: Added 2026-10-10 (0003b amendment 3 d1): with `removed`, the account's name (shown "<name> (Account removed)"), since its row in the accounts list is gone.

cloid.description: The client order id gcx journals before sending. A venue order without it was placed outside gcx.

imported.description: 0004 amendment 3 d7: an order placed outside gcx that gcx took into its book on a change, for its whole life (its id stays ext:<the venue's order id>). Absent otherwise.

change.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 726 (e)): the last change a request asked for since the runtime started (a modify, a take-profit or stop-loss edit) and how it ended: `applied` once the exchange took it (or at once when nothing rests there to change), `reverted` when the exchange refused it and the order is back as it was, `failed` when the order went into repair. Absent while the outcome is not known, for an order nobody changed, and after a restart. The panel's snackbar waits for its own request's.

cancelOnly.description: 0004 amendment 3 d3: an order placed outside gcx that gcx can cancel but not change as it was placed (a take-profit trigger, a position TP/SL, a grouped leg, another copy's order): no pencil, no Modify. Absent otherwise.

changedAt.description: Optional C52 last admitted own display change, in epoch milliseconds; never a ledger sequence.

chartAlgo.description: Optional factual legacy DCA exec_inst equivalence from generated-order membership or its actual iteration bracket; not inferred from a row botId label.

gridStart.description: A grid's start order: bought or sold at once at the price, its limit only the grid's edge it may not pass; the chart draws its fills, not a line at that edge. Absent on every other row and on older runtimes.

chartSeq.description: Optional visual-facts revision; includes indexed related-child changes without changing order state.

modifyChainId.description: Shared by every order of a modify chain; the list keys the row by modifyChainId, else id.

unarmed.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 728 (a), 729 (b)): a take-profit or stop-loss leg whose parent order has not filled in full: a plan, nothing of it on the exchange. The lists leave it out (Open orders and History); its parent's details show it. Absent once the parent has filled, and from older runtimes (an older panel lists the leg as before).

plannedExits.description: Added 2026-10-18 (MH 729 (r) (a)): on a parent order that ended (cancelled) before it filled in full, how many take-profits and stop-losses it had planned; their legs are `unarmed` and no list rows, so History's +TP/+SL tags read this. Absent on every other row, and from older runtimes.

restOf.description: Added 2026-10-05 (0026 d5): a send of an order's rest, shown as its own row with the id `<order id>:rest<k>` (k = 1, 2, …): the order's id, which an action on the row acts on. Its size, fills, average and fee are that send's; the order's first row (its id) is its sends before the first rest. A person's take-profit or stop-loss keeps its role; a bot's rest is role and type `exit`. Absent on every other row, and from older runtimes.

role.description: liquidation and adl (added 2026-10-05, decision 0016 Amendment 3 d4): in a bot's activity, its share of an order the exchange filled, with `whole`.

level.description: The averaging level when role is avg.

botId.description: Set on a bot-owned order: the list offers the bot, not Cancel.

type.description: liquidation and adl (added 2026-10-05, decision 0016 Amendment 3 d4): a fill the exchange made, one closed row per account and venue order (id `liquidation:<sourceId>:<venue order id>`), with `botsShare`.

status.description: Never moves backwards; a backwards upsert is refused and reported.

reason.description: Why an order is unknown, rejected or failed to trigger. On a closed order whose `closeReason` is `rejected`, the exchange's own words unchanged (the raw message; absent for an order never placed or unfilled, where the exchange said nothing). On an order in repair: the engine's code, or, when the exchange refused the order and gave words (a take-profit, a stop-loss, a fired stop, an error gcx does not recognise), those words unchanged, or, when the exchange cancelled it, its cancel reason (`margin`, `liquidation`, `venue`); `why` is then our explanation (before 2026-10-05, ruling 203, always the code).

why.description: An order in repair: the repair as a sentence for the person, the text the notification says (when the exchange refused the order in words goodcryptoX named, its error type instead, ruling 203; when goodcryptoX refused it itself, `refusalBy` is `gcx` and the sentence says the order was never placed, ruling 570), in the person's language (the `language` setting; English when none is chosen or the language has no text for it). Absent when the order is not in repair. Added 2026-10-05 (ruling 203): also on a closed order whose `closeReason` is `rejected` (refused by the exchange, never placed, or unfilled): our explanation of the error, goodcryptoX's error type for the refusals it named, else the generic one; before it, such a row had no `why` and a reader ignores it.

refusalBy.description: Added 2026-10-16 (ruling 570): on a closed order whose `closeReason` is `rejected`, `reason` is goodcryptoX's own words, not the exchange's: it refused the order before signing it (an instrument it does not trade, a market order it could not price because the book could not be read) or could not sign it; the words start "not sent: ". Also, since the same day (batch-533-578 finding 1), on an order in repair (`status` `unknown`) whose `reason` is such words: a stop that fired and could not be priced. Absent (the default, and on every older row): `reason` is the exchange's words. A reader that does not know it shows `reason` as before.

repairCause.description: Optional factual engine REPAIR code, such as failed-to-trigger after a definite venue refusal or unknown after an ambiguous send. Display metadata only: status, actions and retries keep their lifecycle meaning. Absent when not in REPAIR and on older rows; absent readers keep the previous presentation.

nativeTriggerState.description: Optional positive venue phase of the native stop's current attempt, read from the incremental accepted-event index, seeded by the place reply and promoted by fills. A subsequent triggered account-stream update for an already accepted attempt does not update this fact. Display metadata only; no change to engine state, actions or retries. Absent on older records or without a supported positive fact; readers retain the existing fallback.

custody.description: internal: a trigger gcx watches and sends itself.

resting.description: In the venue's book now (venue truth). The order book dots show resting orders that are not triggers.

triggerPrice.description: Absent until a trailing order with an activation price is active.

waitingTriggerPrice.description: Current admitted stop seed while waiting for trailing activation, including waiting distance edits. The immutable initialTriggerPrice keeps its creation meaning. Absent after activation and on older runtimes; not an active path sample.

held.description: A send gcx holds for the person (0013 ruling 1; status sending): why, only for an order that opens or adds to a position. stopped: gcx stopped before sending it (the next start sends it); disk: the disk is full; maintenance: Hyperliquid was in maintenance when it was due (it goes by itself when the maintenance ends). POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/send-now sends it, cancel ends it. Added 2026-10-04; absent on older rows and on every send not held.

waiting.description: Added 2026-10-05 (0003 Amendment 2 d2, d8): rate-address, Hyperliquid's request allowance for this order's account is used up, and the order (or its cancel) waits its turn: the account sends one action every 10 seconds, in the order they were made. Nothing is refused; Cancel removes a waiting order at once. Added 2026-10-05 (0003 Amendment 3 d5): upgrade-gate, Hyperliquid takes only post-only orders for a few minutes after its upgrade; the order waits and is sent again every 10 seconds until taken (no `ahead`). Absent otherwise and from older runtimes.

ahead.description: With `waiting`: how many of the account's actions go before this one.

trailAnchorPrice.description: Optional admitted trailing distance basis: current engine extreme while trailing, configured Start or recorded placement price while waiting. Display only; never inferred from rounded stop or current tick. Absent on older runtimes.

improveOnlyPrice.description: Latest admitted waiting improve-only activation, updated by accepted waiting edits and retained after trailing begins. Display only; absent on older runtimes or ordinary trailing orders.

trailStart.description: Original configured trailing Start from the admitted order state. null positively means Auto; absent means unavailable on an older runtime or not a trailing order. Independent of computed activationPrice.

improveOnly.description: Actual manual trailing improve-only state, when available.

trailPhase.description: Engine-recorded trailing phase; absent on older runtimes.

trailStartedAt.description: Display-only timestamp of the admitted wait-to-trail activation output for the current trailing revision. Later stop moves retain it; re-arming removes it. Absent for immediately trailing orders and older runtimes; never inferred from a path point or creation time.

trailStartedPointId.description: Display-only id of the admitted trail point that began the current trailing revision, disambiguating activations with the same timestamp. Re-arming removes it. Optional on older runtimes and absent for immediately trailing orders; never authorizes an action.

firedAt.description: The engine-recorded trigger timestamp, when one exists; absence is not an inferred trigger.

expiresAt.description: Time in force as a duration (decision 0004, catalogue P11): when the order is cancelled, milliseconds since the epoch.

size.description: In the base asset; absent when the order was sized in quote (cost).

builderFee.description: Added 2026-10-17 (0004 amendment note): the part of `fee` that is gcx's platform fee (the fills' builder fee, valued as `fee` is), so the exchange's own part is `fee` − `builderFee`. Absent when none of the row's fills names one (a fill recorded before it was kept, or one the venue charged none on, such as a spot buy); `fee` is then the whole fee.

trailGain.description: Added 2026-10-28 (0040 amendment 6): on a grid's trailing exit, its own `gain` as the grid row's `trailing` sums it; what it earned against a limit at its level (`price`) = trailGain + the maker rate × price × filled. Absent on every other order and from older runtimes

createdAt.description: Milliseconds since the epoch. An exit leg nothing has sent yet carries its parent's (a take-profit or stop-loss of an order the person made) or the time its position's take-profit and stop-loss were attached.

placedAt.description: A bot's take-profit, stop-loss or level re-sized or re-levelled by a later send of the same order: when the latest of those sends went (ms). The chart starts the order's line there, as goodcryptoX drew each re-size's new order (MH 285). Absent before such a send, on a person's order and from older runtimes: the line starts at createdAt.

closedAt.description: When the order closed (ms): closed by its fills, the exchange's time of its latest fill (0016 amendment 5; recorded before it: when gcx recorded it); a liquidation or ADL row, its last fill's exchange time; an earlier send of a rest series, when its next send left; any other close (a cancel, a refusal), when gcx recorded it.

whole.description: Added 2026-10-05 (decision 0016 Amendment 3 d4): on a bot's liquidation or adl row, the sum of the sizes of the fills it was charged in; `size` below it is shown "Partially attributed".

botsShare.description: Added 2026-10-05 (decision 0016 Amendment 3 d4): on a liquidation or adl row, what the bots on the coin were charged of it, net (each bot's held size × the fill ÷ the exchange's net position, a bot on the other side counting against; MH 214 (b)); the rest is the person's. Absent when no bot was charged.

order-row.decimal.description: A plain non-negative decimal string. Never a JSON number.

order-row.signed.description: A plain decimal string, negative allowed. Never a JSON number.

build.description: The runtime build stamp; a page compiled for another build reloads once.

ledgerId.description: Minted when the ledger is created; a backup restore or an import mints a new one.

seq.description: The ledger seq this event reflects; the ledger head for topics that are not ledger views (ticks, balances, leverage, candles). Never goes back within one ledger id, except coin-icons: its seq is the icon cache's own counter, restarting with the runtime; since is ignored and every subscribe gets a full snapshot.

data.description: The topic's own frame, as the topic's schema defines it.

panel-socket.topic.description: The topic string, parameters included, as the panel subscribes it: `orders`, `positions`, `bots`, `my-trades` (data: list-frame.schema.json; `my-trades` the take-profit and stop-loss on positions and orders, decision 0011), `account-state` (data: lists-api.schema.json#/$defs/accountState), `balances` (data: balances-frame.schema.json), `ticks/<instrumentId>` (data: tick-frame.schema.json, one instrument's last price and mark, the last one first), `ticks` (the same for every watched instrument; deprecated, removed in the release after V1), `leverage/<sourceId>/<instrumentId>` (data: leverage-topic.schema.json), `candles/<instrumentId>/<resolution>` (data: chart-api.schema.json#/$defs/bar, the forming bar), `book/<instrumentId>/<rung>` with rung `finest`, `5m2`, `5m5`, `4`, `3` or `2` (data: book-frame.schema.json), `trades/<instrumentId>` (data: trades-frame.schema.json, a replay first), `md-state/<instrumentId>` (data: md-state-frame.schema.json), `asset-ctx/<instrumentId>` (data: asset-ctx-frame.schema.json), `ta/<instrumentId>/<interval>` (data: ta-rating-frame.schema.json, the TA rating of a period a DCA bot waits on), `runtime` (data: runtime-topic.schema.json, the process's state and the start-up checks still pending), `coin-icons` (data: a snapshot {epoch, versions}, then updates {coin, version}; every subscribe starts with the full snapshot, since is ignored, and seq is the icon cache's own counter, restarting with the runtime), and the demo accounts' `demo/orders`, `demo/positions`, `demo/bots`, `demo/account-state` and `demo/balances` (the same data; docs/panel/demo-accounts.md); the Trade page holds the market-data topics only while the block showing them is on screen. The runtime refuses a topic it does not serve.

position-row.title: Position row
position-row.description: One venue position as the `positions` topic carries it. A flat position stays with size "0". Total PnL = realizedPnlSinceFlat + unrealizedPnl + funding. Mirrors src/panel/model/frames.ts (PositionRow). See decision 0007 part 2 §9.1.

id.description: Includes the side in hedge mode.

fundingSinceChange.description: Funding since the position's last change of size, the exchange's own figure; paid negative, received positive. Added 2026-10-06: absent from an older runtime's row.

returnOnEquity.description: Optional venue ROE ratio (not percent), including zero. Older rows omit it; display/sort falls back to entry margin.

botId.description: The first bot of `bots`: the row's bot badge.

bots.description: The bots that hold a part of this position and how much each holds (base units; a running bot's open cycle, its close in flight, or a bot stopped without closing that still holds it); empty for a position nobody's bot holds. The person's part is the size less their sum, never below zero (ruling 397). Absent from a runtime older than 2026-10-09.

name.description: Optional already-held bot name; absent from older runtimes or an unnamed bot. No Bots subscription is needed.

botMismatch.description: The bot's own position differs from the venue's.

openedAt.description: When the position opened, from an opening among the fills the runtime has seen. Absent when it has seen none (a position already open when it first read the account): unknown, never the time of the read. Optional since 2026-10-11; a row of an older runtime always has it.

contributors.description: Origins of open own-trades books, not allocated venue size. Absent means legacy attribution.

position-row.forcedClose.description: C66 144: display-only facts from existing admitted liquidation/ADL fills in the preceding 24 hours. No live size, entry, leverage or margin is fabricated. pnl is canonical closed PnL less priced fee; absent for unpriced fee. Partial binding requires positive fill-stream episode evidence; absent/false is unknown or a later episode. Older liquidation records without position metadata yield no fact.

proposal-api.list.description: GET /api/v1/proposals: the proposals waiting, oldest first.

proposal-api.proposal.description: One proposal waiting for you, as GET /api/v1/proposals lists it: the key that proposed it, the order command as the form will show it, when it came (Unix milliseconds).

proposal-api.propose.description: POST /api/v1/proposals: the agent's own `requestId` (new for each proposal, the same when retrying: the same body answers the same proposal, another body 409), and the order command. The command's own `requestId` is not kept, nor `expected`; `overrides` are kept empty: you decide on warnings in the form. A `close` is refused (422): propose a reduce-only order instead.

oneOf.description: POST /api/v1/bots (decision 0016 §7.2, slice L2): create a DCA bot on one account and instrument. Leverage and margin mode are set on the exchange before the bot starts (0016 d7); after that the exchange's value wins. A person, or a trading key within its limits (0016 Amendment 1 B80). Answers 200 {id, warning?} (`warning`, a sentence, only when a TA bot on spot that a sell signal can arm is created while the coin for a full sell ladder is not free or could not be read), 422 {rejected, text}, 409 a requestId reused with another body, 503 a process state.

marginMode.description: Catalogue A7: isolated unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the mode of the position the account holds on the instrument, else isolated.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier; catalogue A7: 5x unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the leverage of the position the account holds on the instrument, else 5x.

name.description: The person's name for the bot (catalogue E11). Added in B8.

note.description: The person's note on the bot (catalogue E11; 500 characters as 0007 d22's notes). Added in B8.

notify.description: The bot's notification switches from the start (0009 d2), journaled with it; absent, every switch on from the entry. Added in B8.

anyway.description: Additive (MH 2026-10-05, audit line 14): a venue read the create needs failed (the API wallet's expiry; on spot, the coin a short bot sells), or, since MH 690 (d), an order of the ladder is beyond the venue's price band or a spot short lacks the coin, and the person saw the warning: the bot is created anyway. Without it a person's create is answered 422 `unread` with the warning and nothing is set or journaled; a trading key's create is never asked and carries the warning in its answer.

kind.description: Absent means DCA, preserving older create bodies.

oneOf.description: 0040 Grid botCreate

marginMode.description: Catalogue A7: isolated unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the mode of the position the account holds on the instrument, else isolated.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier; catalogue A7: 5x unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the leverage of the position the account holds on the instrument, else 5x.

name.description: The person's name for the bot (catalogue E11). Added in B8.

note.description: The person's note on the bot (catalogue E11; 500 characters as 0007 d22's notes). Added in B8.

notify.description: Grid notification switches, journaled from creation: activation, finish, PnL and range on by default; orders off (0040 d21).

anyway.description: Additive (MH 2026-10-05, audit line 14): a venue read the create needs failed (the API wallet's expiry; on spot, the coin a short bot sells), or, since MH 690 (d), an order of the ladder is beyond the venue's price band or a spot short lacks the coin, and the person saw the warning: the bot is created anyway. Without it a person's create is answered 422 `unread` with the warning and nothing is set or journaled; a trading key's create is never asked and carries the warning in its answer.

proposal-api.proposeBot.description: Propose a DCA or Grid create body for a person to review. Nothing trades before Launch. Shares the existing twenty waiting proposals per key.

pulse.title: Pulse
pulse.description: One install's daily usage record (decision 0020 d16; RULINGS_FOR_MH section 21): one per install per UTC day, sent to our reports server through the same Worker, the same switch (reports.auto) and the same install reference as cases. Two closed shapes: the record (reports on) and the heartbeat (reports off: the install reference and the date, nothing else). Never a balance, an address, an order or gcx's version. Passes the last check of d4.5 like a case. Version 1; a new field is additive and optional and needs a schema addition, never a policy.

dashboard.description: The Dashboard was opened that day (active user): the panel's POST /api/v1/usage/dashboard set the day's row.

where.description: Where gcx runs (decision 0024 d15), under the same switch as the rest of the record. Optional, added in the build that follows the Worker's deploy: a record without it is as valid as ever. Never the browser's full user agent, the computer's name, the screen, the language, the time zone or gcx's version.

shell.description: mac: the Mac app's helper runs the runtime; windows: the Windows app's helper (GCXTray.exe) does; docker: the image (GCX_SHELL=docker); node: gcx started by hand or by the person's own unit. A later shell adds its own value.

os.description: System name and release, as case.schema.json header.os, e.g. darwin 25.1.0.

arch.description: The chip type, as case.schema.json header.arch.

browser.description: The family of the browser that last opened the Dashboard that day, reduced at once from its User-Agent (the agent is never stored or sent); absent on a day the Dashboard did not open.

keyStoreLocked.description: A start that day went on with gcx's key store not yet open (unlock-retry): its unlock was slow or failed. Optional, absent on a day every start opened it in time; under the same switch as the rest of the record, and sent only after the Worker's deploy that learns it.

resources.description: What gcx's runtime process uses when the record is built (decision 0030 amendment 3 section 3), under the same switch as the rest of the record. Optional: a record without it is as valid as ever.

rssMb.description: Its resident memory, in whole MB.

cpuSeconds.description: The processor time it used since it started (user and system), in whole seconds.

uptimeSeconds.description: The time since it started, in whole seconds.

venues.description: One entry per venue or chain with something to say; demo accounts and testnet never counted.

venue.description: hyperliquid today; solana and others when built.

live.description: A bot ran or an order of gcx's rested on this venue at any moment of the day (active trader, wide).

created.description: The person or their agent created a bot or an order on this venue that day; a bot's own orders do not count (active sender, narrow).

volume.description: Per quote currency: the sum of price x size of the day's fills of orders gcx placed on this venue, summed with Dec, exact, fees excluded.

quote.description: The instruments' quote asset, e.g. USDC.

oneOf.description: The heartbeat (section 21 (5)): reports are off; this install exists and sends nothing else.

pulse.day.description: The UTC day the record covers.

pulse.install.description: The install reference of case.schema.json header.install: the first 32 hex digits of SHA-256("gcx-case-install:" + installId).

pulse.tier.description: The tier the copy says it is (0030 amendments 1 and 2), as case.schema.json header.tier, so a record from an internal tester is told from one that touches production. Optional: absent when the copy reads none; on the heartbeat too.

runtime-api.attentionDone.description: POST /api/v1/attention/done (decision 0016 Amendment 2 d10; 0003 Amendment 2 d8): a person's Done on a row of the Dashboard's Needs your attention section, of either kind, journaled once as attention.done so every device hides it. key: the row's (a position row's `bot-row.schema.json` attention.key, an allowance row's `runtime-topic.schema.json` attention.key). 200 {accepted: true}; 403 for a key; 503 {error} when the journal could not be written.

runtime-api.attentionSilence.description: Added with 0028 d27.4 (RULINGS 356 b): POST /api/v1/attention/silence, a person's Silence on an item's hourly reminders (Telegram's button and the panel's), journaled once as attention.silence so every device agrees. key: the item's (`items[].key` on the runtime topic's attention rows and on GET /api/v1/bots/{id}). The item stays open, on the Dashboard and on the bot's page, its hold unchanged; a new episode of it has a new key and is reminded again. 200 {accepted: true}; 403 for a key; 503 {error} when the journal could not be written.

oneOf.description: POST /api/v1/bots (decision 0016 §7.2, slice L2): create a DCA bot on one account and instrument. Leverage and margin mode are set on the exchange before the bot starts (0016 d7); after that the exchange's value wins. A person, or a trading key within its limits (0016 Amendment 1 B80). Answers 200 {id, warning?} (`warning`, a sentence, only when a TA bot on spot that a sell signal can arm is created while the coin for a full sell ladder is not free or could not be read), 422 {rejected, text}, 409 a requestId reused with another body, 503 a process state.

marginMode.description: Catalogue A7: isolated unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the mode of the position the account holds on the instrument, else isolated.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier; catalogue A7: 5x unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the leverage of the position the account holds on the instrument, else 5x.

name.description: The person's name for the bot (catalogue E11). Added in B8.

note.description: The person's note on the bot (catalogue E11; 500 characters as 0007 d22's notes). Added in B8.

notify.description: The bot's notification switches from the start (0009 d2), journaled with it; absent, every switch on from the entry. Added in B8.

anyway.description: Additive (MH 2026-10-05, audit line 14): a venue read the create needs failed (the API wallet's expiry; on spot, the coin a short bot sells), or, since MH 690 (d), an order of the ladder is beyond the venue's price band or a spot short lacks the coin, and the person saw the warning: the bot is created anyway. Without it a person's create is answered 422 `unread` with the warning and nothing is set or journaled; a trading key's create is never asked and carries the warning in its answer.

kind.description: Absent means DCA, preserving older create bodies.

oneOf.description: 0040 Grid botCreate

marginMode.description: Catalogue A7: isolated unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the mode of the position the account holds on the instrument, else isolated.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier; catalogue A7: 5x unless chosen. Ruling 88 (a): left out, the leverage of the position the account holds on the instrument, else 5x.

name.description: The person's name for the bot (catalogue E11). Added in B8.

note.description: The person's note on the bot (catalogue E11; 500 characters as 0007 d22's notes). Added in B8.

notify.description: Grid notification switches, journaled from creation: activation, finish, PnL and range on by default; orders off (0040 d21).

anyway.description: Additive (MH 2026-10-05, audit line 14): a venue read the create needs failed (the API wallet's expiry; on spot, the coin a short bot sells), or, since MH 690 (d), an order of the ladder is beyond the venue's price band or a spot short lacks the coin, and the person saw the warning: the bot is created anyway. Without it a person's create is answered 422 `unread` with the warning and nothing is set or journaled; a trading key's create is never asked and carries the warning in its answer.

oneOf.description: POST /api/v1/bots/preview (roadmap B16, release plan B81; decision 0010 d5): the receipt the DCA form shows for these settings, at the runtime's price of the instrument now: the same function the form uses (src/domain/dca/receipt.ts). The create body's account, instrument, leverage and settings, without a requestId; nothing is journaled and nothing is set on the exchange. Any key (scope read). Answers 200 botPreviewAnswer, 422 {rejected, text} (settings the bot cannot run, an instrument not traded on the account), 503 {error} (no price yet, or the account not open).

marginMode.description: As in botCreate; the receipt does not depend on it.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier the approximate margin and the liquidation check use; as at creation, the position's where the account holds one on the instrument, else 5x. Perpetuals only.

kind.description: Absent means DCA, preserving older create bodies.

oneOf.description: 0040 Grid botPreview

marginMode.description: As in botCreate; the receipt does not depend on it.

leverage.description: The integer multiplier the approximate margin and the liquidation check use; as at creation, the position's where the account holds one on the instrument, else 5x. Perpetuals only.

runtime-api.botPreviewAnswer.description: The answer of POST /api/v1/bots/preview: the price it was made at and one receipt per side the bot can enter on (a manual bot its side; a signal bot both). Every amount is a decimal string, exact (the form rounds for display).

price.description: The instrument's price the receipt was made at, as if the entry were made now.

runtime-api.botReceipt.description: One side's receipt (src/domain/dca/receipt.ts Receipt; release plan A27a, B11, B11a, B22): the orders the bot would send, the position's range, the stop's loss, the take-profit's distance from the last level, the margin (perpetuals) or funds (spot), and the liquidation check after each fill (perpetuals).

level.description: 0 for the entry and the exits, n for averaging order n.

pct.description: From the entry's price, in percent, signed.

sent.description: false: under the exchange's minimum order value; shown, not sent.

size.description: From the entry alone to every order sent filled.

price.description: M1: first isolated liquidation on the price path, else the final position; Cross keeps the final-position estimate

runtime-api.dashboardTold.description: Added with MH 220 (0007 Amendment 9 d6): POST /api/v1/dashboard/told, the panel's report that a person saw a Worth a look row: at least half of it in view for five seconds, cumulative within one visit, in a visible, focused window. id: the row's (`dashboard-topic.schema.json` worth[].id). The runtime takes the row's told then (its life P&L, its funding when its words are funding's, the band it shows, the time), once per row per visit; nothing is journaled. 200 {told}: false when the row is not drawn in this visit or was told in it; 403 for a key. dismiss (added with MH 255; absent: false): the person pressed the row's ×: the row is told with what it shows now, even when told already, and the runtime no longer serves it in this visit, on every device; it returns at a later visit only when its situation grows; {told: false} when it is not drawn or was dismissed already. A previous build answers 400 to the field (its body is closed); the panel sends it only to the runtime that serves it.

runtime-api.leverage.description: POST /api/v1/leverage: the exchange's leverage and margin mode for one account and instrument (decision 0007 part 3 decision 8; built in decision 0013 S10). The answer is 200 {accepted: true} once the exchange took it, or 422 {rejected, text}; the leverage topic shows the exchange's state after it, never the request.

runtime-api.loginItem.description: GET /api/v1/login-item answers it; POST /api/v1/login-item turns start at login on or off and answers the system's state after (it may stay off until the system allows it). 404 where nothing starts goodcryptoX at login (a server, Docker, a checkout). The answer is the system's own registration, read each time; on a Mac and Windows the person's "off" is also kept in install.json (0008 amendment 1 d5.5 and its Built notes).

on.description: gcx starts when this user logs in.

runtime-api.margin.description: POST /api/v1/margin (decision 0013 S10; 0003 §2.14): isolated margin added to (positive) or removed from (negative) the account's position on one perpetual, in USDC on the exchange's 0.000001 grid. Sent once, never again without an answer. The answer is 200 {accepted: true} or 422 {rejected, text}.

usdc.description: USDC added (positive) or removed (negative); a decimal string, never a JSON number.

runtime-api.modify.description: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/modify (decision 0004 d10; release plan A65, A67): change an open order. Either a level dragged on the chart and confirmed (decision 0005, item 9), `field` and `price`, or the fields the modify form changes, `changes` (added in A65). What each order may change is goodcryptoX's caps table (docs/reference/orders/primitives.md, Modify); every price, size and duration is a decimal string.

size.description: The order's whole size in the base asset, what filled included.

price.description: A limit's price, a stop-limit's limit price.

distance.description: A trailing stop's distance, in the order's unit (percent or quote).

exits.description: Decision 0004 amendment 2 v4.3 d7 (added 2026-10-18): one Save of the order's Modify form that changes the order and its take-profit and stop-loss is one request. `bracket` is the whole TP/SL block after the Save (exits-command.schema.json, edit), null when both are switched off; `overrides` the exits' warnings sent anyway. The runtime judges the change, then the exits against the order as changed, and journals both in one step, or refuses the request and changes nothing. A person's only: a trading key's request carrying it is refused (key.order). Absent: the change alone, as before; an earlier runtime refuses a body with it.

runtime-api.newsEmail.description: POST /api/v1/news-email: the address the person typed for news about gcx by e-mail (opt-in). The runtime forwards exactly {email} to the website's waitlist and attaches nothing else (no install id, no version). 200 {} when the list took it; 422 {error} for an address that is not one or that the list does not take; 502 {error} when the list did not take it. A person's only, never an access key's.

runtime-api.note.description: POST /api/v1/notes (added with P16, 0007 d22): your note on one order (`order:<id>`, the id its row keeps across a change) or one position (`position:<sourceId>:<instrument>`), plain text of at most 500 characters; empty text removes it. A bot's note is the bot's own (its name and note). A person's only. 200 {}.

runtime-api.notes.description: GET /api/v1/notes (added with P16): every note, by subject.

runtime-api.orderPreviewAnswer.description: The answer of POST /api/v1/orders/preview (decision 0010 d5; added 2026-10-04): what POST /api/v1/orders would judge now, from the same validator with the runtime's own price, balances, position and leverage (docs/reference/orders/validation.md). Nothing is journaled or sent. A trading key's limits are not part of it.

warnings.description: Each refuses a person's order unless its key is in the command's overrides ("send anyway"); a trading key's order is sent with them (RULINGS 75).

receipt.description: What would be sent, figured from the values that can be read, beside any errors (MH 564): null when the size or the price cannot be worked out. An order with no error always has one.

baseSize.description: The size sent, in the base coin, floored to its step.

price.description: The reference price: the limit, the trigger, the expected trailing stop, or the best opposite price for a market order.

funds.description: What it uses: a spot buy its value in the quote, a spot sell its size; perpetuals the margin on what opens new exposure. Absent for a close.

stopType.description: A stop's class by its trigger's side of the last price.

runtime-api.panelDictionary.description: GET /api/v1/i18n/panel/{lang} (added with 0022 L3b): the panel's texts in one language, flat: each key a label's dotted path in English's `locales/en/panel.json` (a word form `type.limit:gen` and a plural phrase `book.orders#few` beside them), each value its text in that language. A key it lacks reads in English. The bundled file of that language with the keys a delivery over the air verified written over it.

runtime-api.passkey.description: One stored passkey: its credential id, the browser that made it, when it was added and last used (milliseconds since the epoch; null, never).

runtime-api.passkeyChallenge.description: POST /api/v1/passkey/challenge: the options for navigator.credentials.create (register) or get (verify), as {publicKey}, binary fields in base64url. One challenge waits per session and purpose, for 2 minutes, used once. 409 at an address other than the panel's name, and for verify when no passkey is stored; 403 for register from a session that has not confirmed while a passkey or passphrase is set.

runtime-api.passkeyOptions.description: The answer to POST /api/v1/passkey/challenge: the publicKey options, the panel's to hand to the browser unchanged once the base64url fields (challenge, user.id, allowCredentials[].id) are bytes.

runtime-api.passkeyRegister.description: POST /api/v1/passkey/register: a new passkey, from the browser's answer to create(); 201 with the stored passkey, and the session counts as checked. Any session while no passkey or passphrase is stored (first run, after a reset); otherwise a confirmed session checked in the last 60 s (403 otherwise). 403 when a check fails.

name.description: The browser that made it, as the panel names it.

runtime-api.passkeyRemove.description: POST /api/v1/passkey/remove: a passkey by its id, or the passphrase ("passphrase"); 204. Needs a check in the last 60 s (403); 404 no such one; 409 the last one while the switch is on.

runtime-api.passkeyState.description: GET /api/v1/passkey (decision 0023 d4): the passkey or passphrase that guards the panel in a browser on this computer. A person's only, never an access key's; answered to a session that has not confirmed yet (`verified` false), without the list.

on.description: The protection switch in Settings › General (Ask for Touch ID, a passkey or a passphrase to open the dashboard; the settings' `localPasskey`).

verified.description: This session may use the panel: the switch is off, or it passed a check and a page of it is on screen now or was within the last 5 minutes.

here.description: The address this request came to: name, http://localhost:<port>, where a passkey works; ip, any other (127.0.0.1), where only the passphrase does.

again.description: Every stored passkey was made at the panel's earlier address (http://gcx.localhost:<port>, before ruling 115), where a browser does not offer it here: the lock makes one anew, after the passphrase where one is set and otherwise with no check first, and it replaces them. Absent: false.

reset.description: On a NAS or a VPS, the line that removes the passkey and the passphrase and signs every browser out: in Docker (GCX_SHELL=docker) `docker exec gcx gcx passkey reset`, typed on the machine (0024 d5.5); elsewhere, pasted into a shell over SSH, this runtime's own Node and script, each quoted, then passkey reset (and --data with the data folder when it is not the system's). Null on a Mac: there the gcx menu in the menu bar has Reset passkey…, which asks for the Mac's password first (RULINGS 162 (b)).

passkeys.description: Only to a verified session: each stored passkey.

runtime-api.passkeySwitch.description: POST /api/v1/passkey/switch: Ask for the passkey on this computer on or off; 204. Needs a check in the last 60 s (403), unless nothing is stored.

runtime-api.passkeyVerify.description: POST /api/v1/passkey/verify: the browser's answer to get(); 204 and the session is confirmed (and checked, for 60 s), 403 when a check fails.

runtime-api.portfolio.description: Holdings (0007 Amendment 5): for each connected main account and sub-account (not a vault, whose figure is your own share, nor a demo account), `vaults` is its total USDC equity in all vaults, `staked` its delegated + undelegated + pending-withdrawal HYPE; each read independently, reused for 5 minutes, null on failure. GET /api/v1/portfolio (added with P8, 0007 d13; since 757 (d) no venue history is read: the account rows lost `readAt`, `start`, `end` and `error` before the first public release, and every change is computed from `snapshots`). Values are decimal strings; null is not known. `pnl` (added with the PnL block, 0007 Amendment 1 d2; since 0007 Amendment 8, rulings 435 b, 437 and 438 a, the realised P&L): in USD, the closed trades after their fees and the funding of each counted account (Include in P&L on, not being removed, not a vault), computed by the runtime from the record it keeps of their fills and funding, never from Hyperliquid's P&L series; over the last 24 hours, 7 x 24, 30 x 24 and all time, each summed in decimal over the accounts whose record is ready (0 when it holds no entry), null while none is. `since`: strictly after the moment (`?since=<ms>`, else the runtime's "since you were last here": the last moment a panel page was on screen before an absence of 30 minutes or more, on any device, rulings 298 and 304 a), `at` the moment itself; null while there is no moment, and for a `?since=` earlier than the 30 days the runtime holds. `partial`: `ok` the accounts whose figure is current, `reading` those still reading their past trades, of the `of` counted. `percent`: the realised P&L's time-weighted return over the same windows, from the runtime's own quarter-hour samples of each account's stablecoin balance, chained between deposits and withdrawals; absent while it is rebuilt; null per window when no return is measurable.

out.description: Live account ids excluded from balances or PnL; absent on older answers means none excluded

reading.description: Added with 0007 Amendment 8: the counted accounts still reading their past trades (none summed while all are). Absent on older answers.

from.description: Added with 0007 Amendment 8: the latest start of a counted account's record after Hyperliquid's 10,000 fills (ms); a window starting before it counts since it. Null when every record is whole; absent on older answers.

percentSince.description: Added with 0007 Amendment 8: a window whose first sample is more than 15 minutes after its start, that sample's time (ms); its percentage counts since it.

percentOut.description: Added with 0007 Amendment 8: the counted accounts in portfolio margin, out of the percentage; their amounts are counted.

led.description: Added with 757 (b): of vaults, the USDC equity in vaults the account leads, which are never part of its balances; null on its own read failure; absent on older answers.

snapshots.description: Added with 757 (d): by account id, each period's base from the runtime's daily snapshots (one a day of each account: each coin's amount and value in USD, at the day's first Dashboard view in which the account's value is wholly known). The base is the snapshot nearest the period's start (24 hours, 7 days and 30 days back; all time: the first snapshot); `whole` when it lies within half a day of that start, an hour for 24 hours (all time: never), else the change counts since `at`. Null: the account has no snapshot yet. Absent on older answers.

runtime-api.previewMessage.description: One check the order meets: the message key (src/domain/orders/messages.ts) and its English text with every placeholder filled.

runtime-api.quit.description: Person-only POST /api/v1/runtime/quit (ruling 110 (b)): the runtime's drained stop, after the answer, where GET /api/v1/runtime says `quit`; 404 elsewhere.

runtime-api.restoreEstimate.description: GET /api/v1/bots/{id}/restore (decision 0016 Amendment 2 d6): "The bot is right"'s market order for the difference between the bots' records on the coin and the exchange's position, estimated from one book read (ruling 141). price: its average on the book; worst: the price its bound allows (the larger of 10 % and 1.5 x the book's reach, no ceiling for a person); cost and fee in the quote; warn: the bound passes 25 % or the book shows less than the size, so the choice needs `anyway`; reduceOnly: it only reduces the exchange's position (perpetuals).

runtime-api.runtimeInfo.description: GET /api/v1/runtime (added with P12's Runtime rows, 0007 d15): where gcx keeps its data (the data folder, a path on this computer) and whether its key store is locked now; with an account open, `watching` (0024 d8.1, added; absent: no account open): what an export would leave unwatched, the warning of Settings › General › Move to another machine. A person's only, never an access key's. 404 from a runtime that does not serve it.

internal.description: C77: true only when the running startup tier is internal; absent on older runtimes means false

demo.description: The installation demo preference, independent of the panel account-view mode

showDataFolder.description: Whether the desktop provider can open its configured data folder

quit.description: Added (ruling 110 (b)): the panel offers Quit goodcryptoX (POST /api/v1/runtime/quit), on the Linux desktop's installed program; absent elsewhere, to a paired device and on older runtimes

installedAt.description: Actual installed build transition time in milliseconds; absent on older installs

apiUrl.description: The runtime's loopback API origin, including its port, for MCP clients and API programs. Present in Docker too; absent from older runtimes.

connector.description: What Settings › API & Agents shows any MCP client: the runtime's loopback address and the program that starts the connector (`gcx mcp`) on this computer, this Node and the connector file; absent in Docker (its paths are the container's), where the file is missing, and from older runtimes.

watching.description: Bots not finished; and, of the person's own open orders (a bot's orders are its bot's, MH 412), the stops and trails gcx triggers itself (`stops`) and every other one, resting, a native stop or waiting for a timer (`orders`). `botStops`: the bots whose own stop-loss gcx triggers itself and is open (one per bot, never its averaging levels); absent from an older runtime means 0.

runtime-api.settings.description: GET /api/v1/settings answers every field; POST /api/v1/settings writes the fields it carries (the selector writes favorites and recents).

telegramTopicsClosed.description: Added with ruling 41: the Telegram bot (its @name) whose optional Turn on topics card the person closed. While it names the linked bot the card is closed (one row under the Telegram switches instead); another bot's card is open. A panel setting only: the runtime makes the topics whenever Threaded Mode turns on, closed or not. Absent reads as null: open.

newsCard.description: The Dashboard's optional e-mail card (Get news about gcx by e-mail); open until the person closes it. Settings › About keeps the field either way. Absent reads as open.

reports.description: Settings › About › Reports to goodcryptoX (decision 0020 d13): auto, gcx sends reports of what went wrong and the daily usage record by itself; off, only the daily sign that this gcx exists (the heartbeat). Absent reads as {auto: true}.

nativeStops.description: Added in P12 (0004 d1): a perpetual's stop-loss with no trigger timeout rests on Hyperliquid as Hyperliquid's own stop order (it fires on the mark price, with Hyperliquid's own slippage); gcx still watches it. Off, the default: gcx watches the last price and sends the stop when it is reached. The panel saves true only after the person confirms the warning. Absent reads as false. An order keeps the choice it was placed with.

profile.description: Added in P12 (0007 d15, §19): the personal profile. `hiddenFields`: the order form's fields it does not show; each goes out at its default (bracket: no take-profit or stop-loss; delay: sent at once; tif: the time-in-force default above; triggerTimeout: none; postOnly, reduceOnly, improveOnly: off; trailStart: trailing from placement). Absent reads as nothing hidden.

liquidationAlert.description: Settings › Trading: close-to-liquidation push alerts for active DCA and Grid perpetual position holders. Absent reads as true. Read at the next price check; off suppresses new approaches, while outside prices still rearm the existing latch.

liquidationAlertPct.description: Distance from the liquidation price, in percent, above 0 (0 would be a second way to say off), inclusive on either side. Absent reads as 10. Read at the next check; a known price outside this distance rearms the existing latch. Previous builds ignore both settings.

bracketReduceOnly.description: Settings › Trading: reduce-only on manual and bot TP/SL and on the Telegram TP/SL buttons, recommended on (MH482, 520). The panel snapshots it at manual send or bot launch, the Telegram buttons at the press; the API never reads it: an API order's or attach's TP/SL without their own `reduceOnly` are reduce-only, and a received value is honoured. Resting orders and running bots retain their choice. Absent reads as true.

language.description: Added with 0022 (localisation): the language of the panel, one of the twenty codes (zh-Hant is Traditional Chinese). null, the default, means not chosen yet: the panel's first visit takes the first of the browser's languages whose language part is one of the twenty (English when none), and saves it. Absent reads as null.

keepAwake.description: Added in R3 (0008 §1.11): with keepAwake on, keep the Mac awake throughout the runtime on mains power (ruling 412 b); on battery or unknown power, while any bot or managed order is not done. Absent reads as true; the runtime topic's `awake` says whether it is held now and why.

localPasskey.description: Added with the local passkey (decision 0023): the protection switch in Settings › General (Ask for Touch ID, a passkey or a passphrase to open the dashboard). GET answers it; POST /api/v1/settings refuses it with 400, since it is turned with POST /api/v1/passkey/switch after a check. Absent reads as true.

proxy.description: P1: all exchange REST and WebSocket connections. Null (the additive default) uses GCX_PROXY if present, otherwise Off. An explicit on/off choice wins over GCX_PROXY. With on true the address must be a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy address, otherwise 400; Off keeps whatever was typed. Applied at the next connection; streams reconnect immediately. Previous builds ignore this field.

logsMaxMb.description: Added by decision 0020 amendment 1: Settings › Storage › Logs › at most … MB. The most the logs (`logs/`, a quarter) and the exchange traffic log (`wire/`, three quarters) take together, in MB (a million bytes); the oldest whole file goes first; applied at once and at each sweep. At least 50. Absent reads as 200.

runtime-api.showDataFolder.description: Person-only POST /api/v1/runtime/show-data-folder opens only the configured folder using the desktop provider; no supplied path. 404 without the capability.

runtime-api.snapshotBase.description: 757 (d): a period's base: when the snapshot was taken (ms), whether it is the period's own start, and each coin the account listed then, its amount in its own units and its value in USD.

runtime-api.updateApply.description: POST /api/v1/updates/apply: the person's Try again, no fields. The runtime answers {state: "updating"} at once, clears a refusal of that build, then downloads and verifies the app, drains and exits 75 at once (no 5 minutes: the person is there); on a server it asks the updater beside it, which pulls the image and restarts the container (the drain on its stop), or says why, the reason then served beside the update still on offer; 409 when GET /api/v1/updates says canUpdate is false.

runtime-api.updateBuilds.description: The answer of GET /api/v1/updates/builds (ruling 114 (c)): for every tier a switch can take (`tiers` of the updates answer), that tier's latest published build, read from its own repository when the person opens Updates from; never a withdrawn one (GitHub's mark or the signed withdrawn list) or a development build. A tier whose list cannot be read or holds no published build has no row; `unread` gives the reason of the first. `tier`, `current` and `builds` (ruling 114 (a): the running tier's whole list) are deprecated: kept unchanged for one release, removed with a migration note in the next; `builds` is empty when the running tier's list cannot be read.

builds.description: The running tier's published builds, newest first. Deprecated (114 (c)).

published.description: When GitHub published it (ISO 8601); absent when GitHub says nothing.

tiers.description: One row per readable tier a switch can take, highest first.

build.description: The tier's newest published build; Beta's is the higher of Beta's and Everyone's, as a switch to Beta installs it.

published.description: When GitHub published it (ISO 8601, date and time); absent when GitHub says nothing.

unread.description: The tiers whose list could not be read, each with the reason (the runtime's own words, for a tooltip, never a line).

runtime-api.updateRollback.description: POST /api/v1/updates/rollback (0024 L10, d7.7): the withdrawn banner's button, no fields; gcx rollback with no build named (d7.1), a person's only. The runtime downloads and checks the previous published build (never a withdrawn one), writes this build as refused, answers {target, warning}, then drains, writes the helper's marker and exits 75; the helper swaps the previous build in. 409 {error} when it cannot (a development build, no helper, no published build below, an update under way, a download or check that failed: nothing changed); 503 {error} while gcx is stopping; 404 where the runtime has no updater.

runtime-api.updateRollbackAnswer.description: The 200 answer of POST /api/v1/updates/rollback and POST /api/v1/updates/tier: the build gcx goes to and the warning to show before it restarts.

target.description: The stamp of the build gcx goes back to.

warning.description: How many internal stops and trails a restart leaves unwatched for a few seconds; for a rollback to a build older than the previous one, or a switch to an older build, a second sentence.

runtime-api.updateTier.description: POST /api/v1/updates/tier (0030 amendment 1 §2.4, rulings 114, 114 (a)): Settings › For developers › Updates from, gcx tier; a person's only. The runtime reads the tier's repository, stages that tier's own copy of its latest build, or of the build named (one of its published builds), newer or older or the same number, answers {target, warning}, then drains and exits 75 for gcx.app's helper to swap it in; the data folder is kept as it is. Going down it writes <data>/updates/switched (the build left), and the second warning line says what waits. Automatic updates then follow that tier, upward only. In Docker nothing is downloaded: the answer is the compose file's image line (updateTierAnswer). 403 {error} above the install's ceiling; 400 {error} for a tier that is none or a build that is not one of the tier's published builds (a withdrawn one is not); 409 {error} where it cannot (no helper, a development build, an update under way, a read, download or check that failed: nothing changed); 503 {error} while gcx is stopping; 404 where the runtime has no updater.

build.description: A build number of the tier's published list; absent: the tier's latest.

runtime-api.updateTierAnswer.description: The 200 answer of POST /api/v1/updates/tier: where a helper swaps the app, the build gcx goes to and the warning to show before it restarts; in Docker, where the image is the program (0030 amendment 1 §4.3), the image line for compose.yaml: the tier's package with its floating tag, or the build's variant.

image.description: The compose file's image, such as ghcr.io/goodcryptoapp/gcx:beta.

runtime-api.updates.description: GET /api/v1/updates (0008 amendment 1 d6, amendment 2 d6; roadmap I7): the updater's state. The runtime reads the latest release from GitHub when it starts and at a read of this route (the panel reads it at each connection) when there is no answer, the last one failed more than a minute ago, or the last is more than 6 hours old; no timer. It keeps the answer in <data>/updates/check.json, so a start serves the last answer at once. Where a helper swaps (gcx.app), a newer build is downloaded and checked by itself (staged) and installed once no panel page has been on screen for 5 minutes. A person's, never an access key's; 404 where the runtime has no updater (the development runtimes).

current.description: The running build's stamp (amendment 2 d1.3): a numbered build such as 3.0.0+2312, a development build such as 3.0.0-dev+2312.a1b2c3d, or a checkout's 3.0.0-dev. The panel compares it at each connection with the one it first received and reloads once when it differs (d6.10).

latest.description: The latest release's stamp (its tag without the v); null before the first check that reached GitHub.

state.description: checking: a check has not answered yet; failed: the last check did not reach an answer (see reason); updating: the runtime is downloading and verifying a newer build (by itself, or after Try again), or draining before it exits 75.

checkedAt.description: When the last check ended, in milliseconds since the epoch.

canUpdate.description: A press installs at once (POST /api/v1/updates/apply, the panel's Try again): a newer release, a helper that swaps the app (gcx.app) or, on a server, the updater beside gcx in the compose file, and not a development build, which reports a release but is never updated by gcx. Also true for a build the helper could not install or put back (refused: never installed again by itself).

reason.description: With failed: why the check failed. With available: why the last update did not install (the download, the checksum, the app's version or signature, the helper's swap, or a put-back of the previous version).

staged.description: Added by 0008 amendment 2 V4: the stamp of the build downloaded and checked (on a server, the image its updater pulled: ruling 28 of 2026-10-18), which installs in the quiet time: no panel page on screen for 5 minutes and no open order within 1 % of its price; absent when none waits.

withdrawn.description: Added by 0024 L10 (d7.7): this build is withdrawn, its own GitHub release marked pre-release after it was found broken. Learned at the usual check, only when latest answers a lower build than this published one (the release list is then read once); kept in check.json and shown at the next start; cleared when a check finds the mark gone or a build not lower. The panel shows "Build N has a problem: go back to the previous build" with one button (POST /api/v1/updates/rollback) on a Mac, the compose line in Docker. Absent: not withdrawn (every older runtime).

previous.description: Added by 0024 L10, only with withdrawn: the stamp of the build the button goes back to (the newest published build below this one, as the release list named it at that check); absent when the list named none.

shell.description: Added by 0024 L10: where gcx runs, the daily record's own value (0024 d15.1): mac under the Mac app's helper, windows under the Windows app's helper (added with it), docker in the image, node otherwise. The panel shows the withdrawn banner's button on a Mac and, in Docker, the compose line in its place and beside an available version. Absent (an older runtime): neither.

tier.description: Added by 0030 amendment 1 TR1b: the running copy's tier, its GCXTier (or GCX_TIER), Everyone with none. Absent: an older runtime.
